title: حِكَايَةُ قَمَرِ الزَّمَانِ
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 894–901 (Night 216, continuing nights-215), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Two verse passages (P897L10–L11, P898L04–L09) are left out of this reading text for now; the gaps are marked. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 216 continues the tale of Qamar al-Zamān. Budūr, reigning as king of the Ebony Isles, takes the stone in the gold as good news of reunion; she seals up the merchants' storehouses and threatens them until the ship's captain sails back and carries off the olive merchant from the orchard in the land of the Magians. Brought before her, Qamar al-Zamān does not know her; she has him bathed and robed, loads him with gifts, and raises him step by step to be treasurer, until he suspects the king of a corrupt purpose and asks leave to go. She tells him she loves him for his beauty, presses him with argument and a run of bawdy verses, and wins his consent to a single time. In bed she has him reach between her thighs, and he finds she is a woman; she laughs and makes herself known, and husband and wife are reunited. Next morning she tells King Armānūs the whole story and that his daughter Ḥayāt al-Nufūs is still a virgin; Armānūs has the story written in gold and offers Qamar al-Zamān his daughter, and Budūr, grateful to her, urges him to accept; and morning overtakes Shahrazād. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.
advisory: This night contains two passages, skipped for now, in which verses that Budūr recites describe sexual acts involving boys.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ السَّادِسَةَ عَشَرَ بَعْدَ الْمِائَتَيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-sādisata ʿashara baʿda al-miʾatayni
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the sixteenth after the two-hundred,
sentences.i: And when it was the two hundred and sixteenth night,
sentences.n: al-sādisata ʿashara, “sixteenth”: as in the nights before, the print has عشر where Classical Arabic would make the second part feminine (ʿashrata) to agree with the night; it is vocalised as printed. The ئ of المائتين is printed.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ الْمَلِكَةَ بُدُورَ لَمَّارَأَتِ الْفَصَّ صَاحَتْ مِنْ فَرْحَتِهَا وَخَرَّتْ مَغْشِيًّا عَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-malikata Budūra lammā raʾati al-faṣṣa ṣāḥat min farḥatihā wa-kharrat maghshiyyan ʿalayhā
sentences.l: She-said: It-has-reached-me, O fortunate king, that the-queen Budūr, when she-saw the-stone, cried-out from her-joy and-fell-down fainted upon-her.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that when Queen Budūr saw the stone she cried out for joy and fell to the ground in a swoon.
sentences.n: The print sets lammā raʾat, “when she saw”, solid as لمارأت; it is kept so, and the hamza of رأت is printed. al-faṣṣ, “the stone”, the gem she lost, which she has just found among the gold in the olive jars; its shadda is printed. min farḥatihā: min marks the cause, “for her joy”; farḥa, “joy”, a noun of the later language beside Classical faraḥ. kharra, “to fall down”. maghshiyyan ʿalayhā, “fainted”, literally “covered over upon her”: the passive participle of ghushiya ʿalayhi, “he swooned”, keeps its masculine form and its ʿalā, which marks the one overcome.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَفَاقَتْ قَالَتْ فِي نَفْسِهَا إِنَّ هٰذَا الْفَصَّ كَانَ سَبَبَ فِرَاقِي مِنْ مَحْبُوبِي قَمَرِ الزَّمَانِ وَلٰكِنَّ هٰذَا بَشِيرُ الْخَيْرِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā afāqat qālat fī nafsihā inna hādhā al-faṣṣa kāna sababa firāqī min maḥbūbī Qamari al-Zamāni wa-lākinna hādhā bashīru al-khayri
sentences.l: And-when she-came-to, she-said in her-soul: Indeed this stone was (the) cause (of) my-parting from my-beloved Qamar al-Zamān; but this (is the) herald (of) the-good.
sentences.i: When she came to herself she said in her heart, “This stone was the cause of my parting from my beloved Qamar al-Zamān; but now it is a herald of good.”
sentences.n: afāqa, Form IV, “to come round, recover one's senses”. qālat fī nafsihā, “she said in her soul”, that is, to herself. firāq min, “parting from”: min marks the one parted from. The stone was the cause because Qamar al-Zamān took it from her as she slept, and a bird carried it off. bashīr, “bringer of good news, herald”. The print writes lākinna without the long ā; it is pointed with a dagger alif.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَعْلَمَتِ السِّتَّ حَيَوٰةَ النُّفُوسِ بِأَنَّ وُجُودَهُ بِشَارَةُ الِاجْتِمَاعِ
sentences.tr: thumma aʿlamati al-Sitta Ḥayāta al-Nufūsi bi-anna wujūdahu bishāratu al-ijtimāʿi
sentences.l: Then she-informed the-Lady Ḥayāt al-Nufūs of-that its-finding (was the) good-tidings (of) the-coming-together.
sentences.i: Then she told the Lady Ḥayāt al-Nufūs that its finding was the good tidings of their reunion.
sentences.n: The print has وجودة, a misprint for وجوده, corrected here. aʿlama, Form IV, “to inform”: the verb takes bi- for what one is told of, here the clause bi-anna …, “of the fact that …”. The print spells the name حيوٰة with wāw and a dagger alif, the old spelling of ḥayāh, “life”: Ḥayāt al-Nufūs, “Life of Souls”, is the Ebony King's daughter whom Budūr has married for show. wujūd, “finding, being found”, a verbal noun; -hu is the stone. bishāra, “good tidings”; ijtimāʿ, Form VIII, “coming together”, that is, with her husband.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ جَلَسَتْ عَلَى كُرْسِيِّ الْمَمْلَكَةِ وَأَحْضَرَتْ رَئِيسَ الْمَرْكَبِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu jalasat ʿalā kursiyyi al-mamlakati wa-aḥḍarat raʾīsa al-markabi
sentences.l: And-when the-morning became-morning, she-sat upon (the) chair (of) the-kingdom and-had-brought (the) captain (of) the-ship.
sentences.i: When morning came she sat on the throne of the kingdom and had the ship's captain brought before her.
sentences.n: aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu, “the morning dawned”, verb and subject from the same root, a stock phrase. kursī al-mamlaka, “the chair of the kingdom”, the throne. aḥḍara, Form IV, “to have brought, summon”. raʾīs, “captain”; its ئ is printed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا حَضَرَ قَبَّلَ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ḥaḍara qabbala al-arḍa bayna yadayhā
sentences.l: And-when he-came, he-kissed the-ground between her-two-hands.
sentences.i: When he came he kissed the ground before her.
sentences.n: qabbala al-arḍa bayna yadayhā, “he kissed the ground between her hands”, the courtly obeisance before a ruler; bayna yaday, “between the two hands of”, means “in front of”. The shadda of قبّل is printed. The narrator says “her”, though the captain sees a king.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ أَيْنَ تَرَكْتَ صَاحِبَ هٰذَا الزَّيْتُونِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat ayna tarakta ṣāḥiba hādhā al-zaytūni
sentences.l: And-she-said: Where did-you-leave (the) owner (of) this olive?
sentences.i: She said, “Where did you leave the owner of these olives?”
sentences.n: al-zaytūn, “olives”, a collective, so hādhā, “this”, is masculine singular. ṣāḥib, “owner, master”.

sentences.t: قَالَ يَامَلِكَ الزَّمَانِ تَرَكْنَاهُ فِي بِلَادِ الْمَجُوسِ وَهُوَ خَوْلِيُّ بُسْتَانٍ
sentences.tr: qāla yā malika al-zamāni taraknāhu fī bilādi al-Majūsi wa-huwa khawliyyu bustānin
sentences.l: He-said: O-king (of) the-age, we-left-him in (the) lands (of) the-Magians, and-he (is the) keeper (of) a-garden.
sentences.i: He said, “O king of the age, we left him in the land of the Magians; he is the keeper of an orchard.”
sentences.n: The print sets yā malika, “O king”, solid as ياملك, kept so; malik al-zamān, “king of the age”, is a courtly address, and it echoes the name Qamar al-Zamān. al-Majūs, “the Magians”, the Zoroastrians, in the tale a city of fire-worshippers. khawlī, “keeper, overseer of an estate or orchard”, a word of the later language; bustān, “garden, orchard”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ إِنْ لَمْ تَأْتِ بِهِ فَلَا تَعْلَمُ مَا يَجْرِي عَلَيْكَ وَعَلَى مَرْكَبِكَ مِنَ الضَّرَرِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu in lam taʾti bihi fa-lā taʿlamu mā yajrī ʿalayka wa-ʿalā markabika mina al-ḍarari
sentences.l: And-she-said to-him: If not you-bring him, then-not you-know what will-run upon-you and-upon your-ship of the-harm.
sentences.i: She said to him, “If you do not bring him, you cannot imagine what harm will come upon you and your ship.”
sentences.n: atā bi-, “to come with”, that is, “to bring”: the verb chooses bi- for what is brought; taʾti is the jussive after lam, and the hamza of تأت is printed. fa-lā taʿlamu …, “then you do not know …”, a threat: what will happen is past your knowing. jarā ʿalā, “to run upon, befall”: ʿalā marks the one it falls on, here with a hint of harm. min al-ḍarari, “of harm”: min tells what kind of thing mā is.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَمَرَتْ بِالْخَتْمِ عَلَى مَخَازِنِ التُّجَّارِ
sentences.tr: thumma amarat bi-al-khatmi ʿalā makhāzini al-tujjāri
sentences.l: Then she-ordered the-sealing upon (the) storehouses (of) the-merchants.
sentences.i: Then she ordered the merchants' storehouses to be sealed,
sentences.n: amara bi-, “to order”: the verb takes bi- for the thing ordered. khatm ʿalā, “sealing upon”, putting the seal on a door so that nothing can be moved in or out. tujjār, plural of tājir, “merchant”; its shadda is printed.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ لَهُمْ إِنَّ صَاحِبَ هٰذَا الزَّيْتُونِ غَرِيمِي وَلِي عَلَيْهِ دَيْنٌ وَإِنْ لَمْ تَأْ تُوابِهِ لَأَقْتُلَنَّكُمْ جَمِيعًا وَأَنْهَبُ تِجَارَتَكُمْ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat lahum inna ṣāḥiba hādhā al-zaytūni gharīmī wa-lī ʿalayhi daynun wa-in lam taʾtū bihi la-aqtulannakum jamīʿan wa-anhabu tijāratakum
sentences.l: and-she-said to-them: Indeed (the) owner (of) this olive (is) my-debtor, and-to-me upon-him (is) a-debt; and-if not you-bring him, I-will-surely-kill-you all, and-I-plunder your-merchandise.
sentences.i: and said to them, “The owner of these olives is my debtor, and he owes me a debt. If you do not bring him, I will kill you all, every one, and plunder your goods.”
sentences.n: gharīm, “debtor”, a word that also means “creditor”; here lī ʿalayhi daynun, “to me upon him is a debt”, settles it: li- marks the one owed, ʿalā the one who owes. The print splits taʾtū bihi, “you bring him”, as تا توابه, with the break inside the verb and bihi run on to it; the tokens are kept as set and vocalised taʾ tū-bihi. la-aqtulannakum, “I will surely kill you”: la- of the oath and the energetic -anna; its shadda is printed. Classical usage would carry the oath form on to the next verb, wa-la-anhabanna; the print has plain wa-anhabu, “and I plunder”, as the spoken language does, and it is vocalised so. tijāra, “trade”, here “merchandise”.

sentences.t: فَأَقْبَلُوا عَلَى الرَّئِيسِ وَوَعَدُوهُ بِأُجْرَةِ مَرْكَبِهِ وَيَرْجِعُ ثَانِيَ مَرَّةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-aqbalū ʿalā al-raʾīsi wa-waʿadūhu bi-ujrati markabihi wa-yarjiʿu thāniya marratin
sentences.l: And-they-came-forward to the-captain, and-promised-him (the) hire (of) his-ship, and-he-returns (a) second time.
sentences.i: So they came to the captain and promised him the hire of his ship if he would go back a second time.
sentences.n: The print has ووعدوة, a misprint for ووعدوه, corrected here. aqbala ʿalā, Form IV, “to come up to, approach”: ʿalā marks the one approached. waʿada bi-, “to promise”: the verb takes the person as object and bi- for what is promised; ujra, “hire, fee”. wa-yarjiʿu, “and he returns”, is loosely joined: it is the condition of the promise, that he go back. thānī marra, “a second time”, the later language's order, with the ordinal before its noun.

sentences.t: وَقَالُوا لَهُ خَلِّصْنَا مِنْ هٰذَا الظَّالِمِ الْغَاشِمِ
sentences.tr: wa-qālū lahu khalliṣnā min hādhā al-ẓālimi al-ghāshimi
sentences.l: And-they-said to-him: Save-us from this oppressor, the-tyrant.
sentences.i: and they said to him, “Rid us of this cruel tyrant!”
sentences.n: khalliṣ, Form II imperative, “set free, rescue”: min marks what one is saved from; its shadda is printed. ẓālim, “oppressor, wrongdoer”, and ghāshim, “tyrannous, high-handed”, make a rhyming pair.

sentences.t: فَنَزَلَ الرَّئِيسُ فِى الْمَرْكَبِ وَحَلَّ قُلُوعَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-nazala al-raʾīsu fī al-markabi wa-ḥalla qulūʿahā
sentences.l: And-went-down the-captain in the-ship and-loosed her-sails.
sentences.i: The captain went down into his ship and set her sails,
sentences.n: nazala fī al-markab, “to go down into the ship”, to go on board. ḥalla, “to untie, loose”: loosing the furled sails is setting sail; its shadda is printed. qulūʿ, plural of qilʿ, “sail”; -hā is the ship, feminine as usual in this tale. فى is spelt with ى.

sentences.t: وَكَتَبَ اللّٰهُ لَهُ السَّلَامَةَ حَتَّى دَخَلَ الْجَزِيرَةَ فِى اللَّيْلِ وَطَلَعَ إِلَى الْبُسْتَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-kataba Allāhu lahu al-salāmata ḥattā dakhala al-jazīrata fī al-layli wa-ṭalaʿa ilā al-bustāni
sentences.l: And-wrote God for-him the-safety, until he-entered the-island in the-night and-went-up to the-garden.
sentences.i: and God decreed him a safe passage, until he came to the island by night and went up to the orchard.
sentences.n: kataba Allāhu lahu al-salāmata, “God wrote safety for him”: what God writes is what He decrees, and li- marks the one it is decreed for. al-jazīra, “the island”, the Magians' land, an island in this tale. ṭalaʿa, “to go up”, from the shore inland. فى is spelt with ى.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ قَمَرُ الزَّمَانِ قَدْ طَالَ عَلَيْهِ اللَّيْلُ وَتَذَكَّرَ مَحْبُوبَتَهُ وَجَلَسَ يَبْكِي عَلَى مَاجَرَى لَهُ وَافْتَكَرَ مَحْبُوبَتَهُ وَأَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna Qamaru al-Zamāni qad ṭāla ʿalayhi al-laylu wa-tadhakkara maḥbūbatahu wa-jalasa yabkī ʿalā mā jarā lahu wa-iftakara maḥbūbatahu wa-anshada yaqūlu
sentences.l: And-Qamar al-Zamān, (it) had grown-long upon-him the-night, and-he-remembered his-beloved, and-sat weeping over what had-befallen him, and-thought-of his-beloved, and-recited, saying:
sentences.i: Now Qamar al-Zamān had found the night long, and he had remembered his beloved and sat weeping over all that had befallen him; and thinking of his beloved, he recited:
sentences.n: kāna … qad ṭāla ʿalayhi al-laylu, “the night had grown long upon him”: Qamar al-Zamān is named first, as topic, and the clause after him has its own subject, the night; ʿalā marks the one it weighs on. tadhakkara, Form V, “to remember”, and iftakara, Form VIII, “to think of, call to mind”, a verb of the later language, say almost the same thing twice. The print sets mā jarā, “what happened”, solid as ماجرى, kept so; jarā li-, “to happen to”: li- marks the one it befalls. anshada yaqūlu brings in the verse.

sentences.t:
وَلَيْلِ كَوَاكِبُهُ لَا تَسِيْر * وَلَاهُوَ مِمَّنْ يُطِيْقُ بَرَاحَا
كَيَوْمِ الْقِيٰمَةِ فِيْ طُوْلِهِ * عَلَىٰ مَنْ يُرَاقِبُ فِيْهِ الصَّبَاحَا
sentences.tr:
wa-laylin kawākibuhu lā tasīr * wa-lā huwa mimman yuṭīqu barāḥā
ka-yawmi al-qiyāmati fī ṭūlihi * ʿalā man yurāqibu fīhi al-ṣabāḥā
sentences.l:
And-(many-a)-night, its-stars not move, * and-not it (is) of-those-who can (a) leaving;
like-(the)-day (of) the-resurrection in its-length * upon one-who watches in-it (for) the-morning.
sentences.i:
Many a night whose stars will not move on, * nor can the night itself depart,
as long as the Day of Resurrection * to one who waits in it for the dawn.
sentences.n: The verses are pointed in the print and copied as printed. The metre is mutaqārib, and the lines rhyme in -āḥā. wa-layl, “and (many a) night”: the wāw that opens a poem with an indefinite noun stands for rubba, “many a”, and takes the genitive. The print points it وَلَيْلِ, with a kasra but no tanwīn; the metre wants wa-laylin, and that is how it is read. tasīr is printed with no final vowel. The print sets wa-lā huwa, “nor is it”, solid as وَلَاهُوَ, kept so. mimman is min + man, “of those who”. aṭāqa, Form IV, “to be able to”; barāḥ, “leaving one's place”, the night that will not go. yawm al-qiyāma, “the Day of Resurrection”, proverbially the longest of days; the print writes القيٰمة with a dagger alif. ʿalā man, “upon one who”: ʿalā marks the one it lies heavy on. rāqaba, Form III, “to watch for”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الرَّئِيسَ دَقَّ الْبَابَ عَلَى قَمَرِ الزَّمَانِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-raʾīsa daqqa al-bāba ʿalā Qamari al-Zamāni
sentences.l: Then indeed the-captain knocked the-door upon Qamar al-Zamān.
sentences.i: Then the captain knocked at Qamar al-Zamān's door.
sentences.n: thumma inna …, “then (indeed) …”, the narrator's way of taking up the thread; the shadda of انّ is printed, as is that of دقّ. daqqa al-bāba ʿalā, “to knock the door on”: ʿalā marks the one inside.

sentences.t: فَفَتَحَ الْبَابَ وَخَرَجَ إِلَيْهِ فَحَمَلَهُ الْبَحْرِيَّةُ وَنَزَلُوا بِهِ إِلَى الْمَرْكَبِ وَحَلُّوا الْقُلُوعَ وَسَارُوا
sentences.tr: fa-fataḥa al-bāba wa-kharaja ilayhi fa-ḥamalahu al-baḥriyyatu wa-nazalū bihi ilā al-markabi wa-ḥallū al-qulūʿa wa-sārū
sentences.l: And-he-opened the-door and-came-out to-him, and-carried-him the-sailors, and-they-went-down with-him to the-ship, and-loosed the-sails and-went.
sentences.i: He opened the door and came out to him, and the sailors picked him up and carried him down to the ship, loosed the sails and set off.
sentences.n: al-baḥriyya, “the sailors”, a collective: the first verb, ḥamalahu, is singular with it, the next ones plural, nazalū, ḥallū, sārū, as the sense goes. nazala bi-, “to go down with”, that is, “to take down”: bi- marks the one taken. The shadda of حلّوا is printed.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَالُوا سَائِرِينَ أَيَّا مًا وَلَيَالِيَ وَقَمَرُ الزَّمَانِ لَايَعْلَمُ مَا سَبَبُ ذٰلِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazālū sāʾirīna ayyāman wa-layāliya wa-Qamaru al-Zamāni lā yaʿlamu mā sababu dhālika
sentences.l: And-not they-ceased travelling days and-nights, and-Qamar al-Zamān not knows what (is the) cause (of) that.
sentences.i: They sailed on for days and nights, and Qamar al-Zamān did not know the reason for it.
sentences.n: The print has ولياني, a misprint for وليالي, corrected here. lam yazal, “he did not cease”, with a participle, “kept on”: sāʾirīna, “travelling”, and its ئ is printed. The print splits ayyāman, “days”, as ايا ما; the two pieces are kept as set and vocalised ayyā-man. layāliya, “nights”, is a diptote, so the accusative has -a and no tanwīn. wa-Qamaru al-Zamāni lā yaʿlamu …, “Qamar al-Zamān not knowing …”, a circumstantial clause; the print sets lā yaʿlamu solid as لايعلم.

sentences.t: فَسَأَلَهُمْ عَنِ السَّبَبِ فَقَالُوا لَهُ أَنْتَ غَرِيمُ الْمَلِكِ صَاحِبِ جَزَائِرِ الْآبَنُوسِ صِهْرِ الْمَلِكِ أَرْمَانُوسَ وَقَدْ سَرَقْتَ مَالَهُ يَا مَنْحُوسُ
sentences.tr: fa-saʾalahum ʿani al-sababi fa-qālū lahu anta gharīmu al-maliki ṣāḥibi Jazāʾiri al-Ābanūsi ṣihri al-maliki Armānūsa wa-qad saraqta mālahu yā manḥūsu
sentences.l: And-he-asked-them about the-cause, and-they-said to-him: You (are the) debtor (of) the-king, lord (of the) Isles (of) the-Ebony, son-in-law (of) the-king Armānūs, and-you-have stolen his-money, O ill-starred-one!
sentences.i: He asked them why, and they said to him, “You are the debtor of the king, lord of the Ebony Isles, son-in-law of King Armānūs, and you have stolen his money, you wretch!”
sentences.n: saʾala ʿan, “to ask about”: ʿan marks what is asked after; the hamza of فسألهم is printed. gharīm, “debtor”, as Budūr called him. ṣāḥib, “master, lord”, and ṣihr, “son-in-law”, are both in apposition to al-malik, “the king”, and so genitive. The ئ of جزائر and the madda of الآبنوس are printed. Armānūs is a diptote, genitive in -a. manḥūs, “ill-omened, wretch”, rhymes with Armānūs.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ وَاللّٰهِ عُمْرِي مَا دَخَلْتُ هٰذِهِ الْبِلَادَ وَلَا أَعْرِفُهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla wa-Allāhi ʿumrī mā dakhaltu hādhihi al-bilāda wa-lā aʿrifuhā
sentences.l: And-he-said: By-God, my-life-long not I-entered this land, and-not I-know-it.
sentences.i: He said, “By God, never in my life have I set foot in this land, nor do I know it.”
sentences.n: The print has هذة, a misprint for هذه, corrected here. wa-Allāhi, “by God”: wa- of the oath, with the genitive. ʿumrī mā …, “my life (long) not …”, that is, “never in my life”, an idiom of the spoken language. bilād, “land, country”, a plural treated as feminine singular: hādhihi, -hā.

sentences.t: فَسَارُوا بِهِ حَتَّى أَشْرَفُوا عَلَى جَزَائِرِ الْآبَنُوسِ وَطَلَعُوا بِهِ عَلَى السِّتِّ بُدُورَ
sentences.tr: fa-sārū bihi ḥattā ashrafū ʿalā Jazāʾiri al-Ābanūsi wa-ṭalaʿū bihi ʿalā al-Sitti Budūra
sentences.l: And-they-went with-him until they-came-in-sight upon (the) Isles (of) the-Ebony, and-went-up with-him upon the-Lady Budūr.
sentences.i: They sailed on with him until they sighted the Ebony Isles, and they brought him up before the Lady Budūr.
sentences.n: sāra bi-, “to travel with”, carry along: bi- marks the one taken. ashrafa ʿalā, Form IV, “to look down on, come in sight of”: ʿalā marks what comes into view. ṭalaʿa bi- … ʿalā, “to go up with … to”, that is, to bring someone up into a great person's presence. The ئ of جزائر and the madda of الآبنوس are printed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَتْهُ عَرَفَتْهُ وَقَالَتْ دَعُوهُ عِنْدَ الْخُدَّامِ لِيَدْخُلُوا بِهِ الْحَمَّامَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾathu ʿarafathu wa-qālat daʿūhu ʿinda al-khuddāmi li-yadkhulū bihi al-ḥammāma
sentences.l: And-when she-saw-him she-knew-him, and-she-said: Leave-him with the-servants so-that-they-may-go-in with-him (to) the-bath.
sentences.i: When she saw him she knew him, and she said, “Leave him with the servants, so that they may take him to the bath.”
sentences.n: The print has رأنه, a misprint for رأته, corrected here; the hamza of رأته is printed. daʿū, imperative plural of wadaʿa, “leave, let”. khuddām, plural of khādim, “servant”. li-yadkhulū, “so that they may go in”: li- of purpose with the subjunctive. dakhala bi-, “to go in with”, that is, “to take in”: bi- marks the one taken; al-ḥammām, “the bath”, is the place entered, without a preposition. Its shadda is printed.

sentences.t: وَأَفْرَجَتْ عَنِ التُّجَّارِ وَخَلَعَتْ عَلَى الرَّئِيسِ خِلْعَةً تُسَاوِي عَشَرَةَ آلَافِ دِينَارٍ
sentences.tr: wa-afrajat ʿani al-tujjāri wa-khalaʿat ʿalā al-raʾīsi khilʿatan tusāwī ʿasharata ālāfi dīnārin
sentences.l: And-she-released from the-merchants, and-robed upon the-captain a-robe-of-honour (that) is-worth ten thousands (of) dinar.
sentences.i: She released the merchants, and invested the captain with a robe of honour worth ten thousand dinars.
sentences.n: afraja ʿan, Form IV, “to release, set free”: ʿan marks those set free, here the merchants and their sealed storehouses. khalaʿa ʿalā, “to bestow (a robe) on”: ʿalā marks the one honoured, and khilʿa, “robe of honour”, is from the same root. sāwā, Form III, “to be worth”. ʿashara ālāf, “ten thousands”: after ʿashara the counted noun is a genitive plural; the madda of آلاف is printed. The shadda of التجّار is printed.

sentences.t: وَدَخَلَتْ تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةَ فِى الْقَصْرِ وَأَعْلَمَتْ حَيَوٰةَ النُّفُوسِ بِذٰلِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-dakhalat tilka al-laylata fī al-qaṣri wa-aʿlamat Ḥayāta al-Nufūsi bi-dhālika
sentences.l: And-she-went-in that night into the-palace, and-informed Ḥayāt al-Nufūs of-that.
sentences.i: That night she went into the palace and told Ḥayāt al-Nufūs of it,
sentences.n: tilka al-laylata, “that night”, an accusative of time. dakhala fī, “to go into”; فى is spelt with ى. aʿlama bi-, “to inform of”: bi- marks what is told. The name is spelt حيوٰة, with dagger alif, as above.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ لَهَا اكْتُمِي الْخَبَرَ حَتَّى أَبْلُغَ مُرَادِي وَأَعْمَلَ عَمَلًا يُؤَرَّخُ وَيُقْرَأُ بَعْدَنَا عَلَى الْمُلُوكِ وَالرَّعَايَا
sentences.tr: wa-qālat lahā uktumī al-khabara ḥattā ablugha murādī wa-aʿmala ʿamalan yuʾarrakhu wa-yuqraʾu baʿdanā ʿalā al-mulūki wa-al-raʿāyā
sentences.l: And-she-said to-her: Conceal the-news until I-reach my-aim and-do a-deed (that) is-chronicled and-is-read after-us to the-kings and-the-subjects.
sentences.i: and said to her, “Keep this secret until I have gained my end, and done a deed that will be set down in the chronicles and read out after us to kings and commoners alike.”
sentences.n: uktumī, imperative feminine of katama, “to keep secret”. ḥattā ablugha … wa-aʿmala, “until I reach … and do”: ḥattā of the end aimed at takes the subjunctive. murād, “wish, aim”. arrakha, Form II, “to date, chronicle”; yuʾarrakhu, “is chronicled”, passive, and its ؤ is printed, as is the hamza of يقرأ. qaraʾa ʿalā, “to read out to”: ʿalā marks the hearers. raʿāyā, plural of raʿiyya, “flock”, the ruler's subjects.

sentences.t: وَحِينَ أَمَرَتْ أَنْ يَدْخُلُوا بِقَمَرِ الزَّمَانِ الْحَمَّامَ فَدَخَلُوا بِهِ الْحَمَّامَ وَأَلْبَسُوهُ لُبْسَ الْمُلُوكِ
sentences.tr: wa-ḥīna amarat an yadkhulū bi-Qamari al-Zamāni al-ḥammāma fa-dakhalū bihi al-ḥammāma wa-albasūhu lubsa al-mulūki
sentences.l: And-when she-ordered that they-go-in with-Qamar al-Zamān (to) the-bath, then-they-went-in with-him (to) the-bath and-clothed-him (in the) dress (of) the-kings.
sentences.i: When she ordered them to take Qamar al-Zamān to the bath, they took him to the bath and dressed him in the clothes of kings.
sentences.n: wa-ḥīna …, fa-…, “and when …, then …”: ḥīna, “at the time when”, is answered by fa-, as lammā often is in the later language. dakhala bi-, “to take in”, as above: bi- marks the one taken. The shadda of the first الحمّام is printed; the second is printed without it. albasa, Form IV, “to clothe”, takes two objects, -hu and lubs, “dress, clothing”.

sentences.t: وَلَمَّا طَلَعَ قَمَرُ الزَّمَانِ مِنَ الْحَمَّامِ صَارَ كَأَنَّهُ غُصْنُ بَانٍ أَوْكَوْكَبٌ يَخْجَلُ بِطَلْعَتِهِ الْقَمَرَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-lammā ṭalaʿa Qamaru al-Zamāni mina al-ḥammāmi ṣāra ka-annahu ghuṣnu bānin aw kawkabun yakhjalu bi-ṭalʿatihi al-qamarāni
sentences.l: And-when came-out Qamar al-Zamān from the-bath, he-became as-if-he (were a) bough (of) ben-tree, or-a-star at-whose-rising are-abashed the-two-moons.
sentences.i: And when Qamar al-Zamān came out of the bath he was like a bough of the ben-tree, or a star whose rising puts both sun and moon to shame.
sentences.n: ṭalaʿa min, “to come out of”. ka-annahu, “as if he (were)”: ka-, like, with anna. ghuṣn bān, “a bough of the bān”, the ben or moringa, a slender tree that stands in verse and rhymed prose for a tall, supple figure. The print sets aw kawkab, “or a star”, solid as اوكوكب, kept so. yakhjalu bi-ṭalʿatihi, “are abashed at his rising”: bi- marks the cause; ṭalʿa, “rising, appearance, face”. al-qamarān, “the two moons”, is the sun and the moon together; the phrase plays on the name Qamar, “moon”. The rhyme falls on bān / al-qamarān.

sentences.t: وَرُدَّتْ رُوحُهُ إِلَيْهِ ثُمَّ تَوَجَّهَ إِلَيْهَا وَدَخَلَ الْقَصْرَ
sentences.tr: wa-ruddat rūḥuhu ilayhi thumma tawajjaha ilayhā wa-dakhala al-qaṣra
sentences.l: And-was-returned his-spirit to-him; then he-went to-her and-entered the-palace.
sentences.i: His spirit came back to him; then he went to her and entered the palace.
sentences.n: ruddat rūḥuhu ilayhi, “his spirit was given back to him”, that is, he revived after his misery and the journey; rūḥ is feminine. The shadda of وردّت is printed; the verb is read as passive, though the spoken language also uses radda intransitively, raddat, “it came back”. tawajjaha ilā, Form V, “to turn towards, go to”: ilā marks the one gone to.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرَتْهُ صَبَّرَتْ قَلْبَهَا حَتَّى يَتِمَّ مُرَادُهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓarathu ṣabbarat qalbahā ḥattā yatimma murāduhā
sentences.l: And-when she-saw-him, she-made-patient her-heart until is-complete her-aim.
sentences.i: When she saw him she schooled her heart to patience until her purpose should be accomplished.
sentences.n: naẓara here takes its object directly, “she saw him”, without ilā. ṣabbara, Form II, “to make patient”, with qalbahā, “her heart”, as object: she held herself back. ḥattā yatimma, “until it be completed”, subjunctive; the shadda of يتمّ is printed.

sentences.t: وَأَنْعَمَتْ عَلَيْهِ بِمَمَالِيكَ وَخَدَمٍ وَجِمَالٍ وَبِغَالٍ وَأَعْطَتْهُ خِزَانَةَ مَالٍ
sentences.tr: wa-anʿamat ʿalayhi bi-mamālīka wa-khadamin wa-jimālin wa-bighālin wa-aʿṭathu khizānata mālin
sentences.l: And-she-bestowed upon-him with-mamluks and-servants and-camels and-mules, and-gave-him a-treasury (of) money.
sentences.i: She bestowed on him mamluks and servants, camels and mules, and gave him a treasury full of money.
sentences.n: anʿama ʿalā … bi-, Form IV, “to bestow on … something”: ʿalā marks the one favoured and bi- the gift. mamālīk, plural of mamlūk, “owned”, the slave-soldiers and pages of a great house; a diptote, so genitive in -a. khadam, “servants”, a collective. jimāl, plural of jamal, “camel”; bighāl, plural of baghl, “mule”. khizāna, “treasury, store”.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ تَزَلْ تُرَقِّي قَمَرَ الزَّمَانِ مِنْ دَرَجَةٍ إِلَى دَرَجَةٍ حَتَّى جَعَلَتْهُ خَازِنْدَارَ
sentences.tr: wa-lam tazal turaqqī Qamara al-Zamāni min darajatin ilā darajatin ḥattā jaʿalathu khāzindāra
sentences.l: And-not she-ceased raising Qamar al-Zamān from step to step, until she-made-him treasurer.
sentences.i: And she went on raising Qamar al-Zamān from rank to rank, until she made him her treasurer.
sentences.n: lam tazal with an imperfect, “she did not cease”, that is, “she kept on”. raqqā, Form II, “to raise, promote”; the shadda of ترقّي is printed. daraja, “step, rank”. khāzindār, “treasurer”, a Persian loan, khazāna-dār, “keeper of the treasure”, the title of the officer of that name at the later sultans' courts. As the object of jaʿala it would be accusative; it is printed without the alif of the indefinite accusative and is pointed with a plain -a.

sentences.t: وَسَلَّمَتْ إِلَيْهِ الْأَمْوَالَ وَأَقْبَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ وَقَرَّبَتْهُ مِنْهَا
sentences.tr: wa-sallamat ilayhi al-amwāla wa-aqbalat ʿalayhi wa-qarrabathu minhā
sentences.l: And-she-handed-over to-him the-moneys, and-turned-toward him, and-drew-him-near to-her.
sentences.i: She handed over the treasure into his keeping, showed him every favour, and kept him close to her.
sentences.n: sallama ilā, Form II, “to hand over to”: ilā marks the one receiving. amwāl, plural of māl, “wealth, money”. aqbala ʿalā, Form IV, here “to turn towards in favour, attend to”. qarraba min, Form II, “to bring near to”: min marks the one he is brought close to. The shaddas of سلّمت and قرّبته are printed.

sentences.t: وَأَعْلَمَتِ الْأُمَرَاءَ بِمَنْزِلَتِهِ فَأَحَبُّوهُ جَمِيعُهُمْ
sentences.tr: wa-aʿlamati al-umarāʾa bi-manzilatihi fa-aḥabbūhu jamīʿuhum
sentences.l: And-she-informed the-emirs of-his-standing, and-they-loved-him, all-of-them.
sentences.i: She made the emirs aware of his standing, and they loved him, every one of them.
sentences.n: The print has فاحبّوة, a misprint for فاحبّوه, corrected here; its shadda is printed. aʿlama bi-, “to inform of”: bi- marks what they are told. manzila, “rank, standing”. jamīʿuhum, “all of them”, in apposition to the subject of aḥabbū.

sentences.t: وَصَارَتِ الْمَلِكَةُ بُدُورُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ تَزِيدُ لَهُ فِى الْمُرَتَّبَاتِ وَقَمَرُ الزَّمَانِ لَايَعْرِفُ مَا سَبَبُ تَعْظِيمِهَا لَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣārati al-malikatu Budūru kulla yawmin tazīdu lahu fī al-murattabāti wa-Qamaru al-Zamāni lā yaʿrifu mā sababu taʿẓīmihā lahu
sentences.l: And-Queen Budūr began every day increasing for-him in the-allowances, and-Qamar al-Zamān not knows what (is the) cause (of) her-honouring him.
sentences.i: Every day Queen Budūr would add to his allowances, and Qamar al-Zamān did not know why she showed him such honour.
sentences.n: ṣāra with an imperfect, “to come to do”, here of what is done again and again: kulla yawmin, “every day”, an accusative of time. zāda li- fī, “to increase for … in”: li- marks the one who gains, fī what is increased. murattabāt, plural of murattab, “allowance, fixed stipend”. The print sets lā yaʿrifu solid as لايعرف. taʿẓīm, Form II verbal noun, “honouring, treating as great”; lahu, with li-, marks the one honoured; فى is spelt with ى.

sentences.t: وَمِنْ كَثْرَةِ الْأَمْوَالِ صَارَ يَهَبُ وَيَتَكَرَّمُ وَيَخْدُمُ الْمَلِكَ أَرْمَانُوسَ حَتَّى أَحَبَّهُ
sentences.tr: wa-min kathrati al-amwāli ṣāra yahabu wa-yatakarramu wa-yakhdumu al-malika Armānūsa ḥattā aḥabbahu
sentences.l: And-from (the) abundance (of) the-moneys he-began giving and-being-generous and-serving the-king Armānūs, until he-loved-him.
sentences.i: And from the abundance of his wealth he took to giving gifts and showing largesse, and he served King Armānūs, until the king loved him;
sentences.n: min kathrati, “from the abundance of”: min marks the cause. wahaba, “to give, make a gift”, here without an object. takarrama, Form V, “to be generous”; its shadda is printed, as is that of احبّه. The subject of aḥabbahu is Armānūs.

sentences.t: وَكَذٰلِكَ أَحَبَّتْهُ الْأُمَرَاءُ وَالْخَوَاصُّ وَالْعَوَامُّ وَصَارُوا يَحْلِفُونَ بِحَيَوٰتِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-ka-dhālika aḥabbathu al-umarāʾu wa-al-khawāṣṣu wa-al-ʿawāmmu wa-ṣārū yaḥlifūna bi-ḥayātihi
sentences.l: And-likewise loved-him the-emirs and-the-elite and-the-common-people, and-they-began swearing by-his-life.
sentences.i: and so too the emirs loved him, and the great and the common folk, and they took to swearing by his life.
sentences.n: aḥabbathu, “(they) loved him”, is feminine singular, as a verb may be before a plural of things or of people taken as a group; its shadda is printed. khawāṣṣ, “the elite, the intimates”, and ʿawāmm, “the common people”, are a fixed pair. ḥalafa bi-, “to swear by”: bi- marks what one swears by. The print spells بحيوٰته with wāw and dagger alif, as in the name Ḥayāt al-Nufūs.

sentences.t: كُلَّ ذٰلِكَ قَمَرُ الزَّمَانِ يَتَعَجَّبُ مِنْ تَعْظِيمِ الْمَلِكَةِ بُدُورَ لَهُ وَيَقُولُ فِي نَفْسِهِ
sentences.tr: kulla dhālika Qamaru al-Zamāni yataʿajjabu min taʿẓīmi al-malikati Budūra lahu wa-yaqūlu fī nafsihi
sentences.l: All that (while), Qamar al-Zamān wonders at (the) honouring (of) Queen Budūr (for) him, and-says in his-soul:
sentences.i: All this while Qamar al-Zamān marvelled at the honour Queen Budūr did him, and said to himself,
sentences.n: The print has نفسة, a misprint for نفسه, corrected here. kulla dhālika, “all that (time)”, is read as an accusative of time, as the spoken language says kull dā, “all this while”; it could also be nominative, kullu dhālika, “all that (happened)”, with what follows as a clause beside it. There is no wa- before Qamar al-Zamān. taʿajjaba min, Form V, “to wonder at”: min marks the cause of wonder; its shadda is printed.

sentences.t: وَاللّٰهِ إِنَّ هٰذِهِ الْمَحَبَّةَ لَا بُدَّ لَهَا مِنْ سَبَبٍ
sentences.tr: wa-Allāhi inna hādhihi al-maḥabbata lā budda lahā min sababin
sentences.l: By-God, indeed this love — no escape for-it from a-cause.
sentences.i: “By God, there must be some cause for this love.
sentences.n: The print has هذة, a misprint for هذه, corrected here. lā budda li- … min, “there is no escape for … from”, that is, “… must have”: li- marks the one bound, min what cannot be avoided. The shadda of بدّ is printed.

sentences.t: وَرُبَّمَا يَكُونُ هٰذَا الْمَلِكُ إِنَّمَا يُكْرِمُنِي هٰذَا الْإِكْرَامَ الزَّائِدَ لِأَجْلِ غَرَضٍ فَاسِدٍ
sentences.tr: wa-rubbamā yakūnu hādhā al-maliku innamā yukrimunī hādhā al-ikrāma al-zāʾida li-ajli gharaḍin fāsidin
sentences.l: And-perhaps this king is only honouring-me this honouring, the-excessive, for-the-sake (of) an-aim corrupt.
sentences.i: Perhaps this king heaps these excessive honours on me only for some lewd purpose.
sentences.n: rubbamā, “perhaps”, with the imperfect. innamā, “only”, limits what follows to the reason given. akrama, Form IV, “to honour”, takes its own verbal noun as an inner object: yukrimunī hādhā al-ikrāma, “honours me with this honouring”. The ئ of الزائد is printed. li-ajli, “for the sake of”: li- marks the purpose. gharaḍ fāsid, “a corrupt aim”: Qamar al-Zamān, who takes the king for a man, suspects that the king wants him for his bed.

sentences.t: فَلَا بُدَّ أَنْ أَسْتَأْذِنَهُ وَأُسَافِرَ مِنْ بِلَادِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lā budda an astaʾdhinahu wa-usāfira min bilādihi
sentences.l: So-no escape (but) that I-ask-leave-of-him and-travel from his-land.
sentences.i: I must ask his leave and depart from his country.”
sentences.n: The print has بلادة, a misprint for بلاده, corrected here. lā budda an, “it is unavoidable that”, “I must”, with the subjunctive. istaʾdhana, Form X of adhina, “to ask leave of”; the hamza of استأذنه is printed. sāfara min, Form III, “to travel away from”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ تَوَجَّهَ إِلَى الْمَلِكَةِ بُدُورَ وَقَالَ لَهَا أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ إِنَّكَ أَكْرَمْتَنِي إِكْرَامًا زَائِدًا
sentences.tr: thumma innahu tawajjaha ilā al-malikati Budūra wa-qāla lahā ayyuhā al-maliku innaka akramtanī ikrāman zāʾidan
sentences.l: Then indeed-he went to Queen Budūr and-said to-her: O king, indeed-you have-honoured-me an-honouring excessive,
sentences.i: Then he went to Queen Budūr and said to her, “O king, you have honoured me beyond measure,
sentences.n: thumma innahu …, “then he …”, the narrator's resumptive formula. The shadda of توجّه is printed. The narrator says “Queen Budūr” and “to her”, while Qamar al-Zamān addresses a king. ikrāman zāʾidan, “an excessive honouring”, the inner object again; the ئ of زائدا is printed.

sentences.t: وَمِنْ تَمَامِ الْإِكْرَامِ أَنْ تَأْذَنَ لِي فِى السَّفَرِ وَتَأْخُذَ مِنِّي جَمِيعَ مَا أَنْعَمْتَ بِهِ عَلَيَّ
sentences.tr: wa-min tamāmi al-ikrāmi an taʾdhana lī fī al-safari wa-taʾkhudha minnī jamīʿa mā anʿamta bihi ʿalayya
sentences.l: and-of (the) completeness (of) the-honouring (is) that you-permit to-me in the-travel and-take from-me all what you-bestowed with-it upon-me.
sentences.i: and it would crown your kindness if you gave me leave to travel, and took back from me all that you have bestowed on me.”
sentences.n: min tamāmi …, “(it is) of the completion of …”: min marks the whole of which the an clause is a part. adhina li- fī, “to give leave to … for”: li- marks the one permitted, fī the thing permitted; the hamza of تأذن is printed, as is that of تأخذ. anʿama bihi ʿalayya, “bestowed it on me”: bi- marks the gift and ʿalā the one favoured, the pattern seen above. The shaddas of منّي and عليّ are printed; فى is spelt with ى.

sentences.t: فَتَبَسَّمَتِ الْمَلِكَةُ بُدُورُ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ مَا حَمَلَكَ عَلَى طَلَبِ الْأَسْفَارِ وَاقْتِحَامِ الْأَخْطَارِ وَأَنْتَ فِي غَايَةِ الْإِكْرَامِ وَتَزَايُدِ الْإِنْعَامِ
sentences.tr: fa-tabassamati al-malikatu Budūru wa-qālat lahu mā ḥamalaka ʿalā ṭalabi al-asfāri wa-iqtiḥāmi al-akhṭāri wa-anta fī ghāyati al-ikrāmi wa-tazāyudi al-inʿāmi
sentences.l: And-smiled Queen Budūr and-said to-him: What carried-you to seeking the-journeys and-plunging-into the-perils, while-you (are) in (the) utmost (of) the-honour and-increase (of) the-favour?
sentences.i: Queen Budūr smiled and said to him, “What drives you to seek out journeys and plunge into perils, when you stand at the height of honour and of ever-growing favour?”
sentences.n: tabassama, Form V, “to smile”. ḥamala ʿalā, “to carry to”, that is, “to drive, induce to”: ʿalā marks what one is driven to. asfār, plural of safar, “journey”; iqtiḥām, Form VIII verbal noun, “plunging headlong into”; akhṭār, plural of khaṭar, “peril”. wa-anta fī …, “while you are in …”, a circumstantial clause. ghāya, “utmost limit”; tazāyud, Form VI verbal noun, “steady increase”; inʿām, “favour, bounty”. Budūr answers in rhymed prose: al-asfār / al-akhṭār, al-ikrām / al-inʿām.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا قَمَرُ الزَّمَانِ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ إِنَّ هٰذَا الْإِكْرَامَ إِذَا لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ سَبَبٌ فَإِنَّهُ مِنْ أَعْجَبِ الْعَجَبِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā Qamaru al-Zamāni ayyuhā al-maliku inna hādhā al-ikrāma idhā lam yakun lahu sababun fa-innahu min aʿjabi al-ʿajabi
sentences.l: And-said to-her Qamar al-Zamān: O king, indeed this honouring, if not is for-it a-cause, then-indeed-it (is) of (the) most-wondrous (of) the-wonder,
sentences.i: Qamar al-Zamān said to her, “O king, if there is no cause for this honour, it is the strangest of strange things,
sentences.n: inna hādhā al-ikrāma idhā …, fa-innahu …, “this honour, if …, then it …”: the noun is set up first, and the condition and its answer follow, with -hu taking it up again. lam yakun lahu sababun, “there is not to it a cause”: li- marks what the cause would belong to. min aʿjabi al-ʿajabi, “of the most wondrous of wonder”, an elative with its own root noun for emphasis.

sentences.t: خُصُوصًا وَقَدْ أَوْلَيْتَنِي مِنَ الْمَرَاتِبِ مَا حَقُّهُ أَنْ يَكُونَ لِلِاخْتِيَارِ مَعَ أَنَّنِي مِنَ الْأَطْفَالِ الصِّغَارِ
sentences.tr: khuṣūṣan wa-qad awlaytanī mina al-marātibi mā ḥaqquhu an yakūna li-al-ikhtiyāri maʿa annanī mina al-aṭfāli al-ṣighāri
sentences.l: especially and-you-have bestowed-on-me of the-ranks what its-due (is) that it-be for-the-old-men, although I (am) of the-children, the-small-ones.
sentences.i: the more so since you have given me ranks that by rights belong to the elders, though I am one of the little children.”
sentences.n: khuṣūṣan, “especially”, an adverbial accusative, followed by a circumstantial wa-qad clause. awlā, Form IV, “to confer on”, with min marking the kind, as with mā above: “of ranks, what …”. marātib, plural of martaba, “rank, office”. mā ḥaqquhu an …, “that whose due is that …”; the shadda of حقّه is printed. al-ikhtiyār is read here as the later language's ikhtiyār, “old man, elder”, a sense the word took on in Ottoman times, which makes the contrast with al-aṭfāl al-ṣighār and the rhyme ikhtiyār / ṣighār; read as Classical ikhtiyār, “choice”, it would mean “for men of choice”, but that sense is uncertain. maʿa annanī, “although I”, literally “with (the fact) that I”. min al-aṭfāl al-ṣighār, “of the little children”, a modest exaggeration: he means he is young.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ الْمَلِكَةُ بُدُورُ سَبَبُ ذٰلِكَ أَنِّي أُحِبُّكَ لِفَرْطِ جَمَالِكَ الْفَائِقِ وَبَدِيعِ حُسْنِكَ الرَّائِقِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu al-malikatu Budūru sababu dhālika annī uḥibbuka li-farṭi jamālika al-fāʾiqi wa-badīʿi ḥusnika al-rāʾiqi
sentences.l: And-said to-him the-queen Budūr: (The) cause (of) that (is) that-I love-you for-(the)-excess (of) your-beauty the-surpassing and-(the)-wonder (of) your-loveliness the-clear.
sentences.i: Queen Budūr said to him, “The reason is that I love you for your surpassing beauty and the rare, bright loveliness of you.
sentences.n: She answers the question he has just put: why the king should heap such favours on him. sababu dhālika annī …, “the cause of that is that I …”: the anna clause is the predicate. li-farṭi, “for the excess of”: li- gives the reason. fāʾiq, “surpassing”, and rāʾiq, “clear, limpid, pleasing”, make the rhyme; their ئ is printed, as is the shadda of احبّك. badīʿ ḥusnika, “the wonder of your loveliness”, the adjective set before its noun in an iḍāfa.

sentences.t: وَإِنْ مَكَّنْتَنِي مِمَّا أُرِيدُهُ مِنْكَ أَزِدْكَ إِكْرَامًا وَعَطَاءً وَإِنْعَامًا وَأَجْعَلْكَ وَزِيرًا عَلَى صِغَرِ سِنِّكَ كَمَا جَعَلَنِي النَّاسُ سُلْطَانًا عَلَيْهِمْ وَأَنَا فِي هٰذَا السِّنِّ
sentences.tr: wa-in makkantanī mimmā urīduhu minka azidka ikrāman wa-ʿaṭāʾan wa-inʿāman wa-ajʿalka wazīran ʿalā ṣighari sinnika kamā jaʿalanī al-nāsu sulṭānan ʿalayhim wa-anā fī hādhā al-sinni
sentences.l: And-if you-enable-me of-what I-want-it from-you, I-increase-you (in) honouring and-giving and-bestowing, and-I-make-you vizier upon (the) smallness (of) your-age, as made-me the-people sultan over-them, and-I (am) in this the-age.
sentences.i: If you will let me have of you what I want, I will heap on you still more honour, gifts and favour, and make you vizier young as you are, just as the people made me sultan over them at my own age.
sentences.n: makkana, Form II, “to give (someone) power over, let (someone) have”: makkantanī min, “you let me have”, with min for what is granted; the shadda of مكّنتني is printed. mimmā is min + mā. What Budūr wants of him is plain, and she means him to hear it. in … azidka … wa-ajʿalka: both verbs of the answer are jussive after in, “if”. ikrām, ʿaṭāʾ, inʿām, “honouring, giving, bestowing”, three verbal nouns in rhyme, accusatives of specification after zāda, “to give more”. ʿalā ṣighari sinnika, “upon the smallness of your age”, that is, “young as you are”: ʿalā of concession. The shaddas of سنّك and السنّ are printed. sinn, “age”, is feminine in Classical usage; hādhā al-sinn treats it as masculine, as the later language does.

sentences.t: وَلَا عَجَبَ الْيَوْمَ فِي رَآسَةِ الْأَطْفَالِ
sentences.tr: wa-lā ʿajaba al-yawma fī riʾāsati al-aṭfāli
sentences.l: And-no wonder today in (the) headship (of) the-children.
sentences.i: And today it is no wonder for children to rule.
sentences.n: lā ʿajaba, “no wonder”: lā denying the whole kind takes its noun in the accusative without tanwīn. riʾāsa, “headship, rule”, is printed رآسة, with madda, for the usual رئاسة or رياسة; it is kept so. al-aṭfāl, “the children”: she takes up his own words, “I am one of the little children”, and turns them back on him.

sentences.t: وَلِلَّهِ دَرُّ مَنْ قَالَ
sentences.tr: wa-li-llāhi darru man qāla
sentences.l: And-to-God (belongs the) excellence (of) whoever said:
sentences.i: And how well the poet put it:
sentences.n: lillāhi darru …, “to God belongs the milk of …”, that is, the goodness of: the stock phrase of admiration that brings in a quotation.

sentences.t: كَأَنَّ زَمَانَنَا مِنْ قَوْمِ لُوْطٍ * لَهُ شَغَفٌ بِتَقْدِيْمِ الصِّغَارِ
sentences.tr: ka-anna zamānanā min qawmi Lūṭin * lahu shaghafun bi-taqdīmi al-ṣighāri
sentences.l: As-if our-time (were) of (the) people (of) Lot: * to-it (is) a-passion for-(the)-putting-forward (of) the-little-ones.
sentences.i: It is as though our age were one of Lot's people, * it has a passion for putting the young ones first.
sentences.n: The verse is printed with its vowels and is given as printed. The people of Lot, the men of Sodom, stand for those who desire boys. taqdīm al-ṣighār is double: “promoting the young” to high office, and “preferring the young” in bed. shaghaf, “passionate love”, properly love that reaches the heart's membrane (shaghāf); bi- marks what the passion is for. The lines fit Budūr's purpose exactly: a beardless boy made king, and a beardless boy to be made vizier.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ قَمَرُ الزَّمَانِ هٰذَا الْكَلَامَ خَجِلَ وَاحْمَرَّتْ خُدُودُهُ حَتَّى صَارَتْ كَالضِّرَامِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa Qamaru al-Zamāni hādhā al-kalāma khajila wa-iḥmarrat khudūduhu ḥattā ṣārat ka-al-ḍirāmi
sentences.l: And-when heard Qamar al-Zamān this speech, he-was-ashamed and-reddened his-cheeks until they-became like-the-blaze.
sentences.i: When Qamar al-Zamān heard these words he was abashed, and his cheeks flushed until they glowed like a fire.
sentences.n: khajila, “to be ashamed, abashed”. iḥmarra, Form IX, “to turn red”, the form for colours; its shadda is printed. khudūd, plural of khadd, “cheek”: the plural for a pair is usual in the later language and in verse, and the verb is feminine with it. ḍirām, “blaze, fire kindled in brushwood”; ka- gives the likeness.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَا حَاجَةَ لِي بِهٰذَا الْإِكْرَامِ الْمُؤَدِّي إِلَى ارْتِكَابِ الْحَرَامِ بَلْ أَعِيشُ فَقِيرًا مِنَ الْمَالِ غَنِيًّا بِالْمُرُوَّةِ وَالْكَمَالِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lā ḥājata lī bi-hādhā al-ikrāmi al-muʾaddī ilā irtikābi al-ḥarāmi bal aʿīshu faqīran mina al-māli ghaniyyan bi-al-murūwati wa-al-kamāli
sentences.l: And-he-said: No need (is) to-me for-this the-honouring the-leading to (the) committing (of) the-forbidden; rather I-live poor of the-wealth, rich in-the-manliness and-the-perfection.
sentences.i: He said, “I have no need of honour that leads to committing what is forbidden. I would rather live poor in wealth and rich in manhood and in virtue.”
sentences.n: lā ḥājata lī bi-, “there is no need to me of”: li- marks the one who has the need, and bi- what is needed. al-muʾaddī ilā, “leading to”, Form II participle of addā; its ؤ and shadda are printed. irtikāb, Form VIII verbal noun, “committing (a sin)”. The rhyme runs ikrām / ḥarām, then māl / kamāl. faqīran mina al-māli, “poor of wealth”: min marks what one lacks. ghaniyyan bi-, “rich in”: bi- marks what one is rich with; the shadda of غنيّا is printed. al-murūwa, “manliness, honour”, is spelt المروة, for Classical murūʾa or muruwwa, and is vocalised murūwa, the later form.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ الْمَلِكَةُ بُدُورُ أَنَا لَا أَغْتَرُّ بِوَرَعِكَ النَّاشِي عَنِ التِّيهِ وَالدَّلَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu al-malikatu Budūru anā lā aghtarru bi-waraʿika al-nāshī ʿani al-tīhi wa-al-dalāli
sentences.l: And-said to-him the-queen Budūr: I not am-deceived by-your-scruple the-arising from the-pride and-the-coquetry.
sentences.i: Queen Budūr said to him, “I am not taken in by your scruples: they spring from vanity and coyness.
sentences.n: ightarra bi-, Form VIII, “to be deceived by”: bi- marks what deceives; the shadda of اغترّ is printed. waraʿ, “scrupulous piety”. al-nāshī ʿan, “arising from”, is the participle nāshiʾ printed without its hamza, as the later language says it; ʿan marks the source. tīh, “pride, haughtiness”; dalāl, “coquetry, playing hard to get”, the airs of a beloved who is sure of being wanted.

sentences.t: وَلِلَّهِ دَرُّ مَنْ قَالَ
sentences.tr: wa-li-llāhi darru man qāla
sentences.l: And-to-God (belongs the) excellence (of) whoever said:
sentences.i: And how well the poet put it:
sentences.n: The same formula as before; this time the print puts a shadda on the lām of God's name (وللّه).

sentences.t:
ذَاكَرْتُهُ عَهْدَ الْوِصَالِ فَقَالَ لِيْ * كَمْ ذَا تُطِيْلُ مِنَ الْكَلَامِ الْمُؤْلِمِ
فَأَرَيْتُهُ الدِّيْنَارَ انَشَدَ قَائِلًا * اَيْنَ الْمَفَرُّ مِنَ الْقَضَاءِ الْمُبْرَمِ
sentences.tr:
dhākartuhu ʿahda al-wiṣāli fa-qāla lī * kam dhā tuṭīlu mina al-kalāmi al-muʾlimi
fa-araytuhu al-dīnāra anashada qāʾilan * ayna al-mafarru mina al-qaḍāʾi al-mubrami
sentences.l:
I-reminded-him (of the) pact (of) the-union, and-he-said to-me: * How-much (is) this (that) you-prolong of the-speech the-painful?
And-I-showed-him the-dinar; he-recited, saying: * Where (is) the-escape from the-decree the-made-firm?
sentences.i:
I spoke to him of the promise of union, and he said to me, * “How long will you keep up this painful talk?”
Then I showed him the dinar, and he recited, * “Where is the escape from fate's fixed decree?”
sentences.n: The verse is printed with its vowels and is given as printed. dhākara, Form III, “to talk over with, remind”, takes the person and the thing as two objects. kam dhā, “how much, this”, that is, “how long”. The second line is printed انَشَدَ, which as it stands is not a good word and breaks the metre (kāmil); the metre and the sense want فأنشد, fa-anshada, “and he recited”, and the English follows that, but the print is kept. The point is in the last half-line: the boy who found talk of love painful yields at the sight of gold, and calls it fate. al-qaḍāʾ al-mubram, “the decree made firm”, the fixed and irrevocable decree of God.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ قَمَرُ الزَّمَانِ هٰذَا الْكَلَامَ وَفَهِمَ الشِّعْرَ وَالنِّظَامَ قَالَ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ إِنَّهُ لَا عَادَةَ لِي بِهٰذِهِ الْفِعَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa Qamaru al-Zamāni hādhā al-kalāma wa-fahima al-shiʿra wa-al-niẓāma qāla ayyuhā al-maliku innahu lā ʿādata lī bi-hādhihi al-fiʿāli
sentences.l: And-when heard Qamar al-Zamān this speech and-understood the-poetry and-the-verse-making, he-said: O king, indeed-it (is that) no habit (is) to-me with-these the-deeds,
sentences.i: When Qamar al-Zamān heard these words and understood the poem and its craft, he said, “O king, I have no habit of such doings,
sentences.n: The print has بهذة, a misprint for بهذه, corrected here. al-shiʿr wa-al-niẓām, “the poetry and the arrangement”: niẓām is the stringing of verse, a rhyming pair with kalām. innahu, “indeed it is (that)”, the pronoun of the fact, introducing what follows. lā ʿādata lī bi-, “I have no custom of”: li- marks the one who has the habit, bi- what it is a habit of. fiʿāl, “deeds, doings”, here as a plural.

sentences.t: وَلَا طَاقَةَ لِي عَلَى حَمْلِ هٰذِهِ الْأَثْقَالِ الَّتِي يَعْجِزُ عَنْ حَمْلِهَا أَكْبَرُ مِنِّي فَكَيْفَ بِي عَلَى صِغَرِ سِنِّي
sentences.tr: wa-lā ṭāqata lī ʿalā ḥamli hādhihi al-athqāli allatī yaʿjizu ʿan ḥamlihā akbaru minnī fa-kayfa bī ʿalā ṣighari sinnī
sentences.l: and-no strength (is) to-me for carrying these the-burdens which is-unable to carry-them (one) bigger than-me; so-how (with) me, upon (the) smallness (of) my-age?
sentences.i: nor have I the strength to bear such loads as one bigger than I could not carry. How then should I, young as I am?”
sentences.n: The print has هذة, a misprint for هذه, corrected here. lā ṭāqata lī ʿalā, “I have no power for”: ʿalā marks the task. athqāl, plural of thiql, “burden, weight”: the double sense, of a man's weight on him, is meant, and rhymes with fiʿāl. ʿajaza ʿan, “to be unable to”, as before; akbaru minnī, “one bigger (older) than I”. fa-kayfa bī, “so how with me?”: bi- marks the one whose case is asked about, “how much less I”. The shaddas of منّي and سنّي are printed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ كَلَامَهُ الْمَلِكَةُ بُدُورُ تَبَسَّمَتْ وَقَالَتْ إِنَّ هٰذَا لَشَيْءٌ عُجَابٌ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat kalāmahu al-malikatu Budūru tabassamat wa-qālat inna hādhā la-shayʾun ʿujābun
sentences.l: And-when heard his-speech the-queen Budūr, she-smiled and-said: Indeed this (is) surely-a-thing astonishing!
sentences.i: When Queen Budūr heard what he said, she smiled and said, “This is a wonderful thing indeed!
sentences.n: kalāmahu, the object, comes before the subject al-malika Budūr. tabassama, Form V, “to smile”; its shadda is printed. inna hādhā la-shayʾun ʿujābun, “this is surely an astonishing thing”, are the words of the unbelievers in the Qurʾān (38:5); la- strengthens the predicate after inna, and its fatḥa is printed. ʿujāb is an intensive of ʿajīb, “wondrous”.

sentences.t: كَيْفَ يَظْهَرُ الْخَطَأُ مِنْ خِلَالِ الصَّوَابِ
sentences.tr: kayfa yaẓharu al-khaṭaʾu min khilāli al-ṣawābi
sentences.l: How appears the-error from between the-right?
sentences.i: How can error show itself out of what is right?
sentences.n: khilāl, “the space between”; min khilāli, “from among, out of”. khaṭaʾ, “error”, and ṣawāb, “what is right”; the hamza of الخطأ is printed. ṣawāb rhymes with ʿujāb. Her meaning: your own plea of youth, which you think right, proves you wrong.

sentences.t: إِذَا كُنْتَ صَغِيرًا فَكَيْفَ تَخْشَي مِنَ الْحَرَامِ وَارْتِكَابِ الْآثَامِ وَأَنْتَ لَمْ تَبْلُغْ حَدَّ التَّكْلِيفِ
sentences.tr: idhā kunta ṣaghīran fa-kayfa takhshā mina al-ḥarāmi wa-irtikābi al-āthāmi wa-anta lam tablugh ḥadda al-taklīfi
sentences.l: If you-are little, then-how do-you-fear of the-forbidden and-(the)-committing (of) the-sins, and-you not have-reached (the) limit (of) the-obligation?
sentences.i: If you are a child, how can you fear what is forbidden and the committing of sins, when you have not yet reached the age of responsibility?
sentences.n: takhshā, “you fear”, is printed with final ي for ى; it is the masculine, not the feminine takhshī. khashiya min, “to be afraid of”: min marks what is feared. āthām, plural of ithm, “sin”; its madda is printed. ḥadd al-taklīf, “the limit of obligation”, is the age at which, in the religious law, a person becomes answerable for his acts. ḥarām / āthām rhyme.

sentences.t: وَلَا مُؤَاخَذَةَ فِي ذَنْبِ الصَّغِيرِ وَلَا تَعْنِيفَ
sentences.tr: wa-lā muʾākhadhata fī dhanbi al-ṣaghīri wa-lā taʿnīfa
sentences.l: And-no calling-to-account (is) in (the) sin (of) the-little-one, and-no rebuke.
sentences.i: and no child is called to account for a sin, nor scolded for it.
sentences.n: muʾākhadha, Form III verbal noun, “taking to task, calling to account”; its ؤ is printed. taʿnīf, “harsh rebuke”, rhymes with taklīf. Both are accusative after lā of the whole kind.

sentences.t: فَقَدْ أَلْزَمْتَ نَفْسَكَ الْحُجَّةَ بِالْجِدَالِ وَحَقَّتْ عَلَيْكَ كَلِمَةُ الْوِصَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-qad alzamta nafsaka al-ḥujjata bi-al-jidāli wa-ḥaqqat ʿalayka kalimatu al-wiṣāli
sentences.l: So you-have-bound your-self (to) the-proof by-the-disputing, and-has-come-true upon-you (the) word (of) the-union.
sentences.i: You have argued yourself into a corner, and the sentence of union has fallen due on you.
sentences.n: alzama, Form IV, “to make binding on”, takes two objects: “you have bound the proof on yourself”, that is, your own argument convicts you. bi- marks the means, al-jidāl, “disputation”. ḥaqqat ʿalayka kalimatu …, “the word of … has come true against you”, turns a Qurʾānic phrase used of God's sentence on sinners (ḥaqqat kalimatu al-ʿadhābi, “the word of punishment came true”, 39:71) to union with her; the shadda of وحقّت is printed. jidāl / wiṣāl rhyme.

sentences.t: فَلَا تُظْهِرْ بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ امْتِنَاعًا وَلَا نُفُورًا وَكَانَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ قَدَرًا مَقْدُورًا
sentences.tr: fa-lā tuẓhir baʿda dhālika imtināʿan wa-lā nufūran wa-kāna amru Allāhi qadaran maqdūran
sentences.l: So do-not show after that refusing nor shying-away; and-was (the) command (of) God a-decree decreed.
sentences.i: So show no more refusal or reluctance after this: God's command is a decree that must be fulfilled.
sentences.n: lā tuẓhir, “do not show”, Form IV jussive after lā of prohibition. imtināʿ, “refusing”, Form VIII; nufūr, “shying away, aversion”. wa-kāna amru allāhi qadaran maqdūran is a verse of the Qurʾān (33:38), word for word: kāna there has the sense of “is ever”. The fatḥa on the dāl of قدرا is printed. nufūr / maqdūr rhyme.

sentences.t: فَأَنَا أَحَقُّ مِنْكَ بِخَشْيَةِ الْوُقُوعِ فِى الضَّلَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-anā aḥaqqu minka bi-khashyati al-wuqūʿi fī al-ḍalāli
sentences.l: For-I (am) more-entitled than-you to-(the)-fearing (of) the-falling into the-error.
sentences.i: It is I, not you, who should fear falling into sin.
sentences.n: aḥaqqu min … bi-, “more entitled than … to”: min marks the one compared, bi- the thing one has the better right to. khashya, “fear”; wuqūʿ fī, “falling into”. ḍalāl, “straying, error”, rhymes with wiṣāl. فى is spelt with ى. She speaks as the grown man she passes for.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ أَجَادَ مَنْ قَالَ
sentences.tr: wa-qad ajāda man qāla
sentences.l: And-indeed did-well whoever said: […]
sentences.i: And well did the poet say: […]
sentences.n: A passage is skipped here for now.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ قَمَرُ الزَّمَانِ هٰذَا الْكَلَامَ تَبَدَّلَ الضِّيَاءُ فِي وَجْهِهِ بِالظَّلَامِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa Qamaru al-Zamāni hādhā al-kalāma tabaddala al-ḍiyāʾu fī wajhihi bi-al-ẓalāmi
sentences.l: And-when heard Qamar al-Zamān this speech, was-exchanged the-light in his-face for-the-darkness.
sentences.i: When Qamar al-Zamān heard these words, the light in his face was changed to darkness,
sentences.n: tabaddala X bi-Y, Form V, “X was exchanged for Y”: bi- marks what takes its place. The rhyme falls on al-kalām / al-ẓalām. The shadda of تبدّل is printed.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ إِنَّهُ يُوجَدُ عِنْدَكَ مِنَ النِّسَاءِ وَالْجَوَارِى الْحِسَانِ مَا لَا يُوجَدُ لَهُ نَظِيرٌ فِي هٰذَا الزَّمَانِ فَهَلَّا اسْتَغْنَيْتَ بِذٰلِكَ عَنِّي فَمِلْ إِلَى مَاشِئْتَ مِنْهُنَّ وَدَعْنِي
sentences.tr: wa-qāla ayyuhā al-maliku innahu yūjadu ʿindaka mina al-nisāʾi wa-al-jawārī al-ḥisāni mā lā yūjadu lahu naẓīrun fī hādhā al-zamāni fa-hallā istaghnayta bi-dhālika ʿannī fa-mil ilā mā shiʾta minhunna wa-daʿnī
sentences.l: and-said: O king, indeed-it is-found with-you, of the-women and-the-slave-girls the-beautiful, what not is-found for-it an-equal in this age; so-why-not you-made-do with-that without-me? So-incline to what you-wished of-them, and-leave-me.
sentences.i: and he said, “O king, you have women and fair slave-girls such as have no equal in this age: why not content yourself with them and do without me? Turn to whichever of them you please, and let me be.”
sentences.n: The print has النساو, a misprint for النساء, corrected here. innahu yūjadu, “indeed there is found”: -hu is the pronoun of the matter, “it is the case that”. mina al-nisāʾi … mā lā yūjadu lahu naẓīrun, “of women … such as has no equal”: min names the kind that mā then sums up. The rhyme falls on al-ḥisān / al-zamān. والجوارى is printed with ى for final ي, the edition’s habit, and vocalised as printed. fa-hallā with the perfect, “why did you not …?”, a reproach. istaghnā bi- ʿan, Form X, “to make do with (bi-) and so do without (ʿan)”. fa-mil, “so incline”, imperative of māla ilā, “to lean toward”; its kasra is printed. ماشئت is one word in the print, mā shiʾta, “whatever you wish”; its ئ is printed, as are the shaddas of فهلّا and عنّي. daʿnī, “leave me”, imperative of wadaʿa.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ إِنَّ كَلَامَكَ صَحِيحٌ وَلٰكِنْ لَا يَشْتَفِي بِهِنَّ مِنْ عِشْقِكَ أَلَمٌ وَلَا تَبْرِيحٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat inna kalāmaka ṣaḥīḥun wa-lākin lā yashtafī bihinna min ʿishqika alamun wa-lā tabrīḥun
sentences.l: And-she-said: Indeed your-speech (is) true, but not is-cured by-them, from love-of-you, a-pain nor a-torment.
sentences.i: She said, “What you say is true; but no pain or torment of love for you finds any cure in them.
sentences.n: Budūr still plays the king, but the verbs are feminine: the narrator knows who she is. yashtafī bihinna, Form VIII, “to be cured by them”: bi- marks the remedy. min ʿishqika, “from love of you”, says where the pain comes from. The reading is not certain: the same letters could be read man ʿashiqaka, “the one who loves you is not cured by them”, but then alamun wa-lā tabrīḥun is left hanging; the sense is the same either way. tabrīḥ, “torment, the pain of love”. The rhyme falls on ṣaḥīḥ / tabrīḥ. ولكن is spelled without its inner alif and pointed with the dagger alif.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا فَسَدَتِ الْأَمْزِجَةُ وَالطَّبِيعَةُ فَهِيَ لِغَيْرِ النُّصْحِ سَمِيعَةٌ مُطِيعَةٌ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā fasadati al-amzijatu wa-al-ṭabīʿatu fa-hiya li-ghayri al-nuṣḥi samīʿatun muṭīʿatun
sentences.l: And-when are-corrupted the-temperaments and-the-nature, then-it (is), to-other-than the-good-counsel, hearing, obeying.
sentences.i: And when the humours and the nature are corrupted, they will listen to and obey anything but good counsel.
sentences.n: al-amzija, plural of mizāj, the “temperaments” or humours of the old medicine, whose balance makes a person’s nature. fa-hiya, “then it”: fa- answers idhā; hiya takes up al-ṭabīʿa, or both nouns together. li-ghayri al-nuṣḥi: li- marks what the hearing and obeying are given to, “to anything but good counsel”. The rhyme falls on al-ṭabīʿa / samīʿa / muṭīʿa.

sentences.t: فَاتْرُكِ الْجِدَالَ وَاسْمَعْ قَوْلَ مَنْ قَالَ
sentences.tr: fa-utruki al-jidāla wa-ismaʿ qawla man qāla
sentences.l: So-leave the-arguing and-hear (the) saying (of) whoever said:
sentences.i: So leave off arguing, and hear what the poet has said:
sentences.n: utruk, imperative of taraka, “to leave”, takes a kasra before the article: fa-utruki al-jidāla. The rhyme falls on al-jidāl / qāl.

sentences.t: اَمَا تَرَى السُّوقَ قَدْ صُفَّتْ فَوَاكِهُهُ * لِلتِّينِ قَوْمٌ وَلِلْجُمَّيْزِ اَقْوَامُ
sentences.tr: a-mā tarā al-sūqa qad ṣuffat fawākihuhu * li-al-tīni qawmun wa-li-al-jummayzi aqwāmu
sentences.l: Do-not you-see the-market, (how) have-been-set-in-rows its-fruits? * For-the-fig (are) people, and-for-the-sycamore-fig peoples.
sentences.i: Do you not see the market, its fruits laid out in rows? * Some folk are for the fig, and others for the sycamore-fig.
sentences.n: The verse is pointed in the print and copied as printed. a-mā, “do … not?”: the question’s a- is printed as a bare alif with its fatḥa. ṣuffat, passive of ṣaffa, “to set in rows”. li-al-tīn … wa-li-al-jummayz: li- marks what each party is for, “for the fig some people, for the sycamore-fig others”. al-jummayz, the sycamore-fig of Egypt, a lesser fruit than the true fig. The point is that tastes differ: Budūr argues that a man may prefer men to women. The line rhymes on aqwāmu.

sentences.t: وَقَوْلُ الْآخَرِ
sentences.tr: wa-qawlu al-ākhari
sentences.l: And-(the)-saying (of) the-other:
sentences.i: And another has said:

sentences.t:
وَصَامِتَةِ الْخَلْخَالِ رَنَّ وُشَاحُهَا * فَهَذَا قَدِ اسْتَغْنَى وَذَا يَشْتَكِى الْفَقْرَا
تُرِيدُ سُلُوِّي عَنْكِ جَهْلاً بِحُسْنِهَا * وَمَا كُنْتُ اَرْضَى بَعْدَ اِيْمَانِيَ الْكُفْرَا
وَحَقِّ عِذَارٍ يَزْدَرِي بِعَقَارِهَا * لَمَا خَدَعَتْنِي عَنْكِ غَانِيَةٌ عَذْرَا
sentences.tr:
wa-ṣāmitati al-khalkhāli ranna wushāḥuhā * fa-hādhā qadi istaghnā wa-dhā yashtakī al-faqrā
turīdu suluwwī ʿanki jahlan bi-ḥusnihā * wa-mā kuntu arḍā baʿda īmāniya al-kufrā
wa-ḥaqqi ʿidhārin yazdarī bi-ʿaqārihā * la-mā khadaʿatnī ʿanki ghāniyatun ʿadhrā
sentences.l:
And-(many a)-silent-(of)-the-anklet, rang her-sash: * so-this has-grown-rich, and-that complains-of the-poverty.
She-wants my-consolation away-from-you, in-ignorance, by-her-beauty, * and-not was-I to-accept, after my-faith, the-unbelief.
And-by-the-truth (of a) cheek-down (that) scorns her-wine, * no has-beguiled-me away-from-you a-beauty, a-virgin.
sentences.i:
Many a woman whose anklet is silent while her sash jingles, * the one grown rich, the other crying poverty,
would have me forget you through her beauty, not knowing what she asks; * but I will not take unbelief once I have faith.
By the down upon a cheek that scorns her wine, * no beauty, no virgin, has ever lured me away from you.
sentences.n: The verses are pointed in the print and copied as printed. wa-ṣāmitati, “and many a silent one”: the wa- here stands for rubba, “many a”, and takes the genitive. Her anklet is silent because her leg is full and leaves it no room to move; her sash rings because her waist is slender and it hangs loose: so the one is “rich”, filled, and the other “complains of poverty”, empty. suluww ʿan, “consolation for, forgetting of”. The rhyme falls on al-faqrā / al-kufrā / ʿadhrā, with the long -ā the rhyme gives. īmāniya, “my faith”: the -ī takes a fatḥa for the metre. wa-ḥaqqi, “by the truth of”, an oath, answered by la-mā, “never has …”. ʿidhār is the first down on a youth’s cheek, the mark of the beardless beloved; ʿaqār, “wine”, so pointed in the print (the usual form is ʿuqār): her wine, the woman’s charms, which the youth’s cheek puts to scorn; bi- marks what is scorned. ghāniya, a woman beautiful enough to need no ornament; ʿadhrā for ʿadhrāʾ, “virgin”, without its hamza in the rhyme. The print points عَنْكِ both times with a kasra, “you” as a woman, where the down on the cheek points to a youth; it is kept, and who is addressed is not certain. يَشْتَكِى is printed with ى.

sentences.t: وَقَوْلُ الْآخَرِ
sentences.tr: wa-qawlu al-ākhari
sentences.l: And-(the)-saying (of) the-other:
sentences.i: And another has said:

sentences.t:
يَا فَرِيْدَ الْجَمَالِ حُبُّكَ دِيْنِيْ * وَاخْتِيَارِيْ عَلى جَمِيْعِ الْمَذَاهِبْ
قَدْ تَرَكْتُ النِّسَا لاَجْلِكَ حَتَّى * زَعَمَ النَّاسُ اَنَّنِى الْيَوْمَ رَاهِبْ
sentences.tr:
yā farīda al-jamāli ḥubbuka dīnī * wa-ikhtiyārī ʿalā jamīʿi al-madhāhib
qad taraktu al-nisā li-ajlika ḥattā * zaʿama al-nāsu annanī al-yawma rāhib
sentences.l:
O unique-one (of) the-beauty, love-of-you (is) my-religion * and-my-choice above all the-schools.
I-have-left the-women for-your-sake, until * claimed the-people that-I (am) today a-monk. […]
sentences.i:
O you who stand alone in beauty, love of you is my religion, * my choice above all the schools of faith.
For your sake I have given up women, * until people say I have become a monk. […]
sentences.n: A passage is skipped here for now.

sentences.t: وَقَوْلُ الْآخَرِ
sentences.tr: wa-qawlu al-ākhari
sentences.l: And-(the)-saying (of) the-other:
sentences.i: And another has said:

sentences.t:
تَقُوْلُ لِيْ وَهْيَ غَضْبَى مِنْ تَدَلُّلِهَا * وَقَدْ دَعَتْنِيْ اِلى شَيْءٍ فَمَا كَانَا
اِنْ لَمْ تَنِكْنِيْ نَيْكَ الْمَرْءِ زَوْجَتَهُ * فَلَا تَلُمْنِيْ اِذَا اَصْبَحْتَ قَرْنَانَا
كَاَنَّ اَيْرَكَ مِنْ شَمْعٍ رَخَاوَتُهُ * فَكُلَّمَا عَرَّكْتُهُ رَاحَتِيْ لَانَا
sentences.tr:
taqūlu lī wa-hya ghaḍbā min tadallulihā * wa-qad daʿatnī ilā shayʾin fa-mā kānā
in lam taniknī nayka al-marʾi zawjatahu * fa-lā talumnī idhā aṣbaḥta qarnānā
ka-anna ayraka min shamʿin rakhāwatuhu * fa-kullamā ʿarraktuhu rāḥatī lānā
sentences.l:
She-says to-me, and-she (is) angry from her-coquetry, * and-had she-called-me to a-thing, and-not it-was:
If not you-fuck-me (the) fucking (of) the-man his-wife, * then-do-not blame-me if you-become a-cuckold.
As-if your-prick, from wax (is) its-softness: * so-whenever I-rubbed-it (with) my-palm, it-went-soft.
sentences.i:
She says to me, angry in her wilfulness, * when she had called me to a certain thing and it did not happen:
“If you won’t fuck me the way a man fucks his wife, * don’t blame me if you wake up a cuckold.
Your prick is as soft as if it were made of wax: * every time I rub it with my palm, it goes limp.”
sentences.n: The verses are pointed in the print and copied as printed. wa-hya, “and she”, with the h left vowelless after wa-, as the poets allow. ghaḍbā, “angry” (f.). tadallul, “coquetry, playing the spoilt beloved”. fa-mā kānā, “and it did not come about”: he could not do it; the rhyme falls on kānā / qarnānā / lānā, with the long -ā the rhyme gives. tanik-nī, jussive of nāka, “to fuck”, after lam; nayka al-marʾi zawjatahu, “the fucking of a man his wife”: the verbal noun nayk keeps its object, zawjatahu, in the accusative. aṣbaḥa, “to come to be”, literally “to be by morning”. qarnān, “cuckold”, literally “horned”, a word of the later language. ka-anna ayraka … rakhāwatuhu, “as if your prick, its softness is of wax”. ʿarraktuhu rāḥatī, “I rubbed it, my palm”: rāḥatī, “my palm”, stands loosely beside the verb for what she rubs with; ʿarraka is Form II, “to rub hard”. lāna, “to grow soft”.

sentences.t: وَقَوْلُ الْآخَرِ
sentences.tr: wa-qawlu al-ākhari
sentences.l: And-(the)-saying (of) the-other:
sentences.i: And another has said:

sentences.t:
قَالَتْ وَقَدْ اَعْرَضْتُ عَنْ غِشْيَانِهَا * يَا اَحْمَقًا فِيْ جَهْلِهِ يَتَنَاهَا
لَمْ تَرْضَ مِنْ قُبُلِيْ لِوَجْهِكَ قِبْلَةً * لَنُوَلِّيَنَّكَ قِبْلَةً تَرْضَاهَا
sentences.tr:
qālat wa-qad aʿraḍtu ʿan ghishyānihā * yā aḥmaqan fī jahlihi yatanāhā
lam tarḍa min qubulī li-wajhika qiblatan * la-nuwalliyannaka qiblatan tarḍāhā
sentences.l:
She-said, and-I-had turned-away from covering-her: * O fool, in his-ignorance going-to-the-limit,
not you-accepted, of my-front, for-your-face a-qibla: * we-shall-surely-turn-you (to) a-qibla you-will-be-pleased-with-it.
sentences.i:
She said, when I had turned away from mounting her, * “You fool, who go to the very limit of ignorance!
If my front won’t do you as a qibla for your face, * we shall surely turn you to a qibla that will please you.”
sentences.n: The verses are pointed in the print and copied as printed. ghishyān, “covering”, the act of sex, from ghashiya, “to come upon”. yā aḥmaqan, “O fool”: the accusative with tanwīn calls on any fool, not one already known. yatanāhā, “goes to the limit”, Form VI of nahā: the word ends in alif maqṣūra and is spelled here with a tall alif to match tarḍāhā. qubul, “front”, the woman’s cunt, played against qibla, the direction a Muslim faces in prayer. The second half-line is the Qurʾān’s own words to the Prophet when the qibla was changed, Q 2:144, “so We shall turn you to a qibla that pleases you”; here the new qibla is her backside. la-nuwalliyannaka, “we shall surely turn you”: la- and the energetic -anna make it an oath.

sentences.t: وَقَوْلُ الْآخَرِ
sentences.tr: wa-qawlu al-ākhari
sentences.l: And-(the)-saying (of) the-other:
sentences.i: And another has said:

sentences.t:
جَادَتْ بِكُسٍّ نَاعِمٍ * فَقُلْتُ اِنِّيْ لَمْ اَنِكْ
فَانْصَرَفَتْ قَائِلَةً * يُؤْفَكُ عَنْهُ مَنْ اُفِكْ
اَلنَّيْكُ مِنْ قُدَّامُ فِيْ * هَذَا الزَّمَانِ قَدْ تُرِكْ
وَدَوَّرَتْ لِيْ فَقْحَةً * مِثْلَ اللُّجَيْنِ الْمُنْسَبِكْ
اَحْسَنْتِ يَا سَيِّدَتِيْ * اَحْسَنْتِ لَا فُجِعْتُ بِكْ
اَحْسَنْتِ يَا اَوْسَعُ مِنْ * فُتُوْحِ مَوْلَانَا الْمَلِكْ
sentences.tr:
jādat bi-kussin nāʿimin * fa-qultu innī lam anik
fa-inṣarafat qāʾilatan * yuʾfaku ʿanhu man ufik
al-nayku min quddāmu fī * hādhā al-zamāni qad turik
wa-dawwarat lī faqḥatan * mithla al-lujayni al-munsabik
aḥsanti yā sayyidatī * aḥsanti lā fujiʿtu bik
aḥsanti yā awsaʿu min * futūḥi mawlānā al-malik
sentences.l:
She-was-generous with-a-cunt soft, * and-I-said: Indeed-I not did-fuck.
So-she-turned-away, saying: * Is-turned-away from-it whoever was-turned-away.
The-fucking from (the) front, in * this age, has-been-abandoned.
And-she-turned-round for-me an-arsehole * like the-silver the-molten.
You-did-well, O my-lady! * You-did-well, may-I-not-be-bereaved of-you!
You-did-well, O wider than * (the) conquests (of) our-lord the-king!
sentences.i:
She freely offered me a soft cunt; * I said, “I don’t fuck that way.”
She turned away, saying, * “He is turned from it who is turned away.
Fucking from the front, * in this day and age, is out of use.”
And she turned round to me an arsehole * like molten silver.
Well done, my lady! * Well done, and may I never lose you!
Well done, you who are wider * than the conquests of our lord the king!
sentences.n: The verses are pointed in the print and copied as printed, except يا in the last line, which the print leaves bare and is pointed here. jāda bi-, “to give freely”: the verb chooses bi-, which marks the gift. kuss, “cunt”; lam anik, “I did not fuck”, jussive of nāka after lam: “I am not one who fucks (there)”. The second line takes the words of the Qurʾān, Q 51:9, where it is the truth that the deluded are turned away from: “turned from it is he who is turned”. min quddāmu, “from in front”: quddām is cut off from what would follow it and so takes a ḍamma, like qablu and baʿdu. faqḥa, “arsehole”; lujayn, “silver”; munsabik, “molten, poured out”, Form VII of sabaka. lā fujiʿtu bik, “may I not be bereaved of you”, bik for biki at the rhyme: lā with the perfect makes a wish, and bi- marks the one lost. The rhyme falls on a vowelless -ik throughout. awsaʿu is printed with a ḍamma, where the grammar of the vocative wants the accusative awsaʿa before min; kept as printed. futūḥ, “conquests”, also “openings”, which is the joke.

sentences.t: وَقَوْلُ الْآخَرِ
sentences.tr: wa-qawlu al-ākhari
sentences.l: And-(the)-saying (of) the-other:
sentences.i: And another has said:

sentences.t:
يَسْتَغْفِرُ النَّاسُ بِاَيْدِيهِمْ * وَهُنَّ يَسْتَغْفِرْنَ بِالْاَرْجُلِ
يَا لَهُ مِنْ عَمَلٍ صَالِحٍ * يَرْفَعُهُ اللّٰهُ اِلى اَسْفَلِ
sentences.tr:
yastaghfiru al-nāsu bi-aydīhim * wa-hunna yastaghfirna bi-al-arjuli
yā lahu min ʿamalin ṣāliḥin * yarfaʿuhu Allāhu ilā asfali
sentences.l:
Ask-forgiveness the-people with-their-hands, * and-they (f.) ask-forgiveness with-the-legs.
O for-it, of a-deed righteous, * raises-it God to below!
sentences.i:
Men ask God’s pardon with their hands lifted, * but women ask it with their legs.
Oh, what a righteous deed it is, * which God raises up to the lowest place!
sentences.n: The verses are pointed in the print and copied as printed. yastaghfiru, Form X of ghafara, “to ask forgiveness”, done with hands raised in prayer; the women raise their legs instead. bi- marks the means, “with”. yā lahu min ʿamalin, “O what a deed!”: yā la- of wonder, with min naming what is wondered at. The second half-line turns the Qurʾān, Q 35:10, where the righteous deed is what God raises up to Him; here He raises it “to below”. asfali is printed with a kasra and no tanwīn for the rhyme with al-arjuli. اللّٰهُ is printed with its shadda and dagger alif.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ قَمَرُ الزَّمَانِ مِنْهَا هٰذِهِ الْأَشْعَارَ وَتَحَقَّقَ أَنَّهُ لَيْسَ لَهُ مِمَّا أَرَادَتْهُ فِرَارٌ قَالَ يَا مَلِكَ الزَّمَانِ إِنْ كَانَ وَلَابُدَّ فَعَاهِدْنِي عَلَى أَنَّكَ لَاتَفْعَلُ بِي هٰذَا الْأَمْرَ غَيْرَ مَرَّةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa Qamaru al-Zamāni minhā hādhihi al-ashʿāra wa-taḥaqqaqa annahu laysa lahu mimmā arādathu firārun qāla yā malika al-zamāni in kāna wa-lā budda fa-ʿāhidnī ʿalā annaka lā tafʿalu bī hādhā al-amra ghayra marratin wāḥidatin
sentences.l: And-when Qamar al-Zamān heard from-her these verses, and-made-certain that-he — not (was) for-him from-what she-wanted an-escape, he-said: O king (of) the-age, if it-is (so), and-no way-out, then-covenant-with-me on (this): that-you not do with-me this thing other-than one time,
sentences.i: When Qamar al-Zamān heard these verses from her, and saw for certain that there was no escaping what she wanted of him, he said, “O king of the age, if it must be, then give me your pledge that you will do this thing with me only once,
sentences.n: The print has هذة, a misprint for هذه, corrected here. laysa lahu … firārun, “there was not for him … an escape”: the subject of laysa, firār, “flight, escape”, is held back to the end of the clause; mimmā is min mā, “from what”, and the -hu of arādathu, “she wanted it”, takes up mā. The narrator says “she”, though Qamar al-Zamān still thinks he is speaking to a king: yā malika al-zamāni, “O king of the age”. in kāna wa-lā budda, “if it is (so), and there is no help for it”, a set phrase of the later language; the print sets wa-lā budda solid, ولابدّ, with its shadda, and lā tafʿalu solid, لاتفعل; both are kept as set. ʿāhada, Form III, “to make a covenant with”: ʿalā marks its terms. faʿala bi-, “to do (something) to (someone)”: bi- marks the one it is done to. ghayra marratin wāḥidatin, “other than one time”, that is, once only.

sentences.t: وَإِنْ كَانَ ذٰلِكَ لَا يُجْدِي فِي إِصْلَاحِ الطَّبِيعَةِ الْفَاسِدَةِ وَبَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ لَا تَسْأَلْنِي فِيهِ عَلَى الْأَبَدِ لَعَلَّ اللّٰهَ يُصْلِحُ مِنِّي مَافَسَدَ
sentences.tr: wa-in kāna dhālika lā yujdī fī iṣlāḥi al-ṭabīʿati al-fāsidati wa-baʿda dhālika lā tasʾalnī fīhi ʿalā al-abadi laʿalla Allāha yuṣliḥu minnī mā fasada
sentences.l: even-if that does-not avail in (the) setting-right (of) the-nature the-corrupt; and-after that do-not ask-me about-it for ever: perhaps God will-set-right of-me what has-gone-bad.
sentences.i: even though it will do nothing to mend a corrupted nature; and after that, never ask it of me again. Perhaps God will set right in me what has gone bad.”
sentences.n: wa-in kāna, “even if, even though”. ajdā, Form IV, “to be of use, avail”: fī marks what it would help. al-ṭabīʿa al-fāsida, “the corrupt nature”: he takes the king's desire for a man as a perversion, and his own consent as a sin. saʾala fī, “to ask (someone) about (a thing)”: fī marks the matter, and -hi is the act; lā with the jussive, tasʾalnī, forbids. Its hamza is printed. ʿalā al-abad, “for ever”, with the negative “never”, a usage of the later language beside Classical abadan. The print sets mā fasada solid as مافسد, kept so; the shadda of لعلّ is printed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ عَاهَدْتُكَ عَلَى ذٰلِكَ رَاجِيًا أَنَّ اللّٰهَ عَلَيْنَا يَتُوبُ وَيَمْحُو بِفَضْلِهِ عَنَّا عَظِيمَ الذُّنُوبِ
