sentences.tr: fa-qālat ʿāhadtuka ʿalā dhālika rājiyan anna Allāha ʿalaynā yatūbu wa-yamḥū bi-faḍlihi ʿannā ʿaẓīma al-dhunūbi
sentences.l: And-she-said: I-covenant-with-you on that, hoping that God toward-us will-turn and-will-wipe-away by-His-bounty from-us (the) great (of) the-sins;
sentences.i: She said, “I give you my pledge on that, hoping that God will turn to us in mercy and of His bounty wipe away our great sins;
sentences.n: ʿāhadtuka, “I have covenanted with you”, the perfect of a pledge made in the speaking. rājiyan, “hoping”, is masculine: Budūr still speaks as the king, though the narrator calls her “she”. tāba ʿalā, “to turn (in mercy) toward”, said of God relenting toward the penitent; ʿalaynā is set before its verb, so that the rhyme falls on yatūbu / al-dhunūbi. bi-faḍlihi, “by His bounty”: bi- marks the means. maḥā ʿan, “to wipe away from”: ʿan marks the one released. ʿaẓīma al-dhunūbi, “the great of sins”, an adjective set in construct before its noun: “our great sins”. The shadda of عنّا is printed.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّ نِطَاقَ أَفْلَاكِ الْمَغْفِرَةِ لَا يَضِيقُ عَنْ أَنْ يُحِيطَ بِنَا وَيُكَفِّرَ عَنَّا مَا عَظُمَ مِنْ هَيِّأٰتِنَا وَيُخْرِجَنَا إِلَى نُورِ الْهُدَى مِنْ ظَلَامِ الضَّلَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-inna niṭāqa aflāki al-maghfirati lā yaḍīqu ʿan an yuḥīṭa binā wa-yukaffira ʿannā mā ʿaẓuma min hayyiʾātinā wa-yukhrijanā ilā nūri al-hudā min ẓalāmi al-ḍalāli
sentences.l: for indeed (the) girdle (of the) spheres (of) the-forgiveness is-not too-narrow for that it-encompass us, and-atone for-us what is-great of our-[sins], and-bring-us-out to (the) light (of) the-guidance from (the) darkness (of) the-straying.
sentences.i: for the circuit of the heavens of forgiveness is not too narrow to take us in, to atone for whatever is grave among our sins, and to bring us out of the darkness of error into the light of guidance.
sentences.n: niṭāq, “girdle”, and so a compass or circuit; aflāk, plural of falak, “celestial sphere”: forgiveness is pictured as a sky whose round has room for every sinner. ḍāqa ʿan, “to be too narrow for”: ʿan marks what it would fail to hold. aḥāṭa bi-, Form IV, “to encompass”: the verb chooses bi-. kaffara ʿan, Form II, “to expiate (sins) on behalf of”: ʿan marks the one atoned for; its shadda is printed. yuḥīṭa, yukaffira and yukhrijanā are all subjunctives after an. The print has هيّأتنا, with its shadda and a printed hamza on alif; the sense wants سيّئاتنا, sayyiʾātinā, “our evil deeds, our sins”, and so it is translated. But more than a dot divides the two, so the print is kept and pointed as its letters allow, hayyiʾātinā, the long ā shown by a dagger alif; as it stands it is no known word, and the reading “our sins” is a guess, though the likeliest one. akhraja ilā … min, Form IV, “to bring out to … from”. The rhymed prose sets light against dark: al-hudā, “guidance”, against al-ḍalāl, “straying, error”.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ أَجَادَوَأَ حْسَنَ مَنْ قَالَ
sentences.tr: wa-qad ajāda wa-aḥsana man qāla
sentences.l: And-indeed did-well and-did-finely the-one-who said:
sentences.i: And how well and how finely the poet put it:
sentences.n: The print spaces this as اجادوا حسن, which read word by word would be “they did well, the beauty of …”; the sense is أجاد وأحسن, ajāda wa-aḥsana, “he did well and did finely”, the stock praise before a quotation, with the wa- and the alif of aḥsana run on to the first word. The print's spacing is kept, and the two tokens are pointed to give ajāda wa-a|ḥsana across the break. man qāla, “the one who said”, the poet, left unnamed. Budūr is still speaking.

sentences.t:
تَوَهَّمَ فِيْنَا النَّاسُ شَيْأً وَصَمَّمَتْ * عَلَيْهِ نُفُوْسٌ مِنْهُمُ وَقُلُوْبُ
تَعَالِيْ نُحَقِّقْ ظَنَّهُمْ لِنُرِيْحَهُمْ * مِنَ الْاِثْمِ فِيْنَا مَرَّةً وَنَتُوْبُ
sentences.tr:
tawahhama fīnā al-nāsu shayʾan wa-ṣammamat * ʿalayhi nufūsun minhumu wa-qulūbu
taʿālī nuḥaqqiq ẓannahum li-nurīḥahum * mina al-ithmi fīnā marratan wa-natūbu
sentences.l:
Imagined about-us the-people a-thing, and-were-set * upon-it souls of-them and-hearts.
Come (f.)! let-us-make-true their-suspicion, so-as-to-relieve-them * of the-sin concerning-us, once, and-(then)-let-us-repent.
sentences.i:
People have imagined something of us, and their souls * and their hearts are set upon it.
Come, let us make their suspicion true, and spare them * the sin of thinking it of us; just once, and then let us repent.”
sentences.n: The verses are pointed in the print and copied as printed. The metre is ṭawīl, and the lines rhyme in -ūbu: qulūbu / natūbu. tawahhama fī, Form V, “to fancy, suspect (something) of”: fī marks the ones suspected. ṣammama ʿalā, Form II, “to be set upon, resolve on”; the verb is feminine with the plural nufūs. minhumu keeps the old long -u of the pronoun for the metre. taʿālī, “come!”, is the feminine imperative: the lines are spoken to a woman, a hint in Budūr's mouth that her listener cannot yet take. nuḥaqqiq, jussive in answer to the imperative, “(and) let us make true”. li-nurīḥahum, li- of purpose with the subjunctive; arāḥa min, Form IV, “to relieve of”. The sin is theirs, the sin of thinking evil of others: once the thing is true, they no longer sin by believing it. The print writes شَيْأً with the hamza on an alif seat, a bare alif without hamza in الْاِثْمِ, and a sukūn on many long vowels; all are kept.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَعْطَتْهُ الْمَوَاثِيقَ وَالْعُهُودَ وَحَلَفَتْ لَهُ بِوَاجِبِ الْوُجُودِ أَنَّهُ لَا يَقَعُ بَيْنَهُمَا وَبَيْنَهُ هٰذَا الْفِعْلُ إِلَّامَرَّةً فِي الزَّمَانِ وَإِنْ أَلْجَاهَا غَرَامُهُ إِلَى الْمَوْتِ وَالْخُسْرَانِ
sentences.tr: thumma aʿṭathu al-mawāthīqa wa-al-ʿuhūda wa-ḥalafat lahu bi-Wājibi al-Wujūdi annahu lā yaqaʿu baynahumā wa-baynahu hādhā al-fiʿlu illā marratan fī al-zamāni wa-in aljāhā gharāmuhu ilā al-mawti wa-al-khusrāni
sentences.l: Then she-gave-him the-pledges and-the-covenants, and-swore to-him by-(the)-Necessary (of) the-Being that-it — not would-happen between-the-two-of-them and-between-him this deed except once in the-time, even-if drove-her her-passion-for-him to the-death and-the-ruin.
sentences.i: Then she gave him pledges and covenants, and swore to him by the Necessary Being that this act would pass between them only once in all time, even if her passion for him should drive her to death and ruin.
sentences.n: mawāthīq, plural of mīthāq, and ʿuhūd, plural of ʿahd, are both “pledge, covenant”, a rhyming pair with al-wujūd. ḥalafa li- … bi-, “to swear to (someone) by”: li- marks the one sworn to, bi- what is sworn by. Wājib al-Wujūd, “the Necessarily Existent”, the philosophers' and theologians' name for God, whose being cannot not be. baynahumā wa-baynahu, “between the two of them and between him”, is what the print says; the sense wants baynahā wa-baynahu, “between her and him”, and the dual may be a slip. It is kept, and translated by the sense. The print sets illā marratan solid as الّامرّة, with both shaddas, kept as set. fī al-zamān, “in time”, that is, ever. aljāhā, “drove her”, is aljaʾahā, Form IV of lajaʾa, with its hamza dropped, a Middle Arabic form; ilā marks where she is driven. gharāmuhu, “his passion”, is read as her passion for him, the pronoun naming the one loved; that reading is the likeliest, not certain. The rhyme falls on al-zamān / al-khusrān.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ مَعَهَا عَلَى هٰذَا الشَّرْطِ إِلَى مَحَلِّ خَلْوَتِهَا لِتُطْفِئَ نِيرَانَ لَوْعَتِهَا وَهُوَ يَقُولُ لَاحَوْلَ وَلَاقُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللّٰهِ الْعَلِيِّ الْعَظِيمِ ذٰلِكَ تَقْدِيرُ الْعَزِيزِ الْعَلِيمِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāma maʿahā ʿalā hādhā al-sharṭi ilā maḥalli khalwatihā li-tuṭfiʾa nīrāna lawʿatihā wa-huwa yaqūlu lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā bi-Allāhi al-ʿAliyyi al-ʿAẓīmi dhālika taqdīru al-ʿAzīzi al-ʿAlīmi
sentences.l: And-he-rose with-her on this condition to (the) place (of) her-privacy, so-that-she-might-quench (the) fires (of) her-burning-love, and-he saying: No power and-no strength except in-God, the-High, the-Mighty; that (is the) ordaining (of) the-Mighty, the-Knowing.
sentences.i: So on this condition he went with her to her private chamber, that she might quench the fires of her longing, saying as he went, “There is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty! This is the ordaining of the Mighty, the All-Knowing.”
sentences.n: maḥall, “place”; khalwa, “privacy, being alone”, and so a room set apart. li-tuṭfiʾa, li- of purpose with the subjunctive of aṭfaʾa, Form IV, “to put out (a fire)”; its hamza is printed. lawʿa, “the burning pain of love”; the rhyme falls on khalwatihā / lawʿatihā. wa-huwa yaqūlu, “he saying”, a circumstantial clause. lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā bi-Allāhi, “there is no power and no strength except in God”, the formula said in the face of what cannot be helped: bi- marks the one in whom all power lies. The print sets lā ḥawla and lā quwwata solid, لاحول ولاقوة, kept as set. dhālika taqdīru al-ʿAzīzi al-ʿAlīmi, “that is the ordaining of the Mighty, the Knowing”, is a phrase of the Qurʾan (6:96, 36:38, 41:12); it rhymes with al-ʿaẓīm.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ حَلَّ سَرَاوِيلَهُ وَهُوَ فِي غَايَةِ الْخَجَلِ وَعُيُونُهُ تَسِيلُ مِنْ شِدَّةِ الْوَجَلِ
sentences.tr: thumma ḥalla sarāwīlahu wa-huwa fī ghāyati al-khajali wa-ʿuyūnuhu tasīlu min shiddati al-wajali
sentences.l: Then he-untied his-trousers, and-he (was) in (the) utmost (of) the-shame, and-his-eyes flowing from (the) intensity (of) the-fear.
sentences.i: Then he undid his trousers in the utmost shame, his eyes streaming for very fear.
sentences.n: ḥalla, “to untie”, here the drawstring of his sarāwīl, “trousers”, a plural form used of the one garment; its shadda is printed. wa-huwa fī …, “he being in …”, and wa-ʿuyūnuhu tasīlu, “his eyes flowing”, are circumstantial clauses. sāla, “to flow”: min marks the cause. The rhyme falls on al-khajal / al-wajal.

sentences.t: فَتَبَسَّمَتْ وَأَطْلَعَتْهُ مَعَهَا عَلَى السَّرِيرِ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ لَا تَرَى بَعْدَ هٰذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ مِنْ نَكِيرٍ
sentences.tr: fa-tabassamat wa-aṭlaʿathu maʿahā ʿalā al-sarīri wa-qālat lahu lā tarā baʿda hādhihi al-laylati min nakīrin
sentences.l: And-she-smiled, and-made-him-go-up with-her onto the-bed, and-said to-him: You-will-not see after this night any disapproval.
sentences.i: She smiled and drew him up with her onto the bed, and said to him, “After this night you will meet with nothing to reproach.”
sentences.n: The print has هذة, a misprint for هذه, corrected here. tabassama, Form V, “to smile”; its shadda is printed. aṭlaʿa, Form IV of ṭalaʿa, “to make (someone) go up”. min nakīrin, “any disapproval”: min after a negative makes it “none at all”. nakīr, “disapproval, censure”: she seems to promise that after this night there will be nothing more for him to object to, as she has sworn; the phrase can also be heard as a sly hint that after tonight he will find nothing wrong in it at all. The rhyme falls on al-sarīr / nakīr.

sentences.t: وَمَالَتْ عَلَيْهِ بِالتَّقْبِيلِ وَالْعِنَاقِ وَالْتِفَافِ سَاقٍ عَلَى سَاقٍ
sentences.tr: wa-mālat ʿalayhi bi-al-taqbīli wa-al-ʿināqi wa-iltifāfi sāqin ʿalā sāqin
sentences.l: And-she-leaned over-him with-the-kissing and-the-embracing and-(the)-twining (of) leg on leg.
sentences.i: And she bent over him with kisses and embraces, twining leg about leg.
sentences.n: māla ʿalā, “to lean over”: bi- marks what she does as she leans. taqbīl, Form II verbal noun, “kissing”; ʿināq, Form III, “embracing”; iltifāf, Form VIII of laffa, “twining round”, here without the article, in construct with sāqin, “a leg”. The rhyme falls on al-ʿināq / sāq.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتْ لَهُ مُدَّ يَدَكَ بَيْنَ فَخِذَيَّ إِلَي الْمَعْهُودِ لَعَلَّهُ يَنْتَصِبُ إِلَى الْقِيَامِ مِنَ السُّجُودِ
sentences.tr: thumma qālat lahu mudda yadaka bayna fakhidhayya ilā al-maʿhūdi laʿallahu yantaṣibu ilā al-qiyāmi mina al-sujūdi
sentences.l: Then she-said to-him: Stretch your-hand between my-two-thighs, to the-familiar-(thing); perhaps-it will-stand-erect to the-standing from the-prostration.
sentences.i: Then she said to him, “Put your hand between my thighs, to the thing you know of; perhaps it will rise from its prostration and stand up straight.”
sentences.n: madda, “to stretch out”, imperative mudda; its shadda is printed. fakhidhayya, “my two thighs”, the dual with -ya, “my”, printed with its shadda. ilā is spelt الي, with a dotted yāʾ, for الى. al-maʿhūd, “the familiar, the known (thing)”, passive participle of ʿahida, used as a noun: what a man is known to have there. Budūr is still playing the king, and bids him reach for the member a king should have. laʿallahu yantaṣibu, “perhaps it will stand erect”: -hu goes back to al-maʿhūd, and intaṣaba, Form VIII, “to stand upright”, is the common word for an erection. ilā al-qiyāmi mina al-sujūdi, “to standing from prostration”, borrows the postures of prayer: the member lies prostrate, and she would have it rise. What his hand finds instead is the joke of what follows. For the reader the word carries a second hint: the place he knew of old, from their nights together. The shadda of لعلّه is printed. The rhyme falls on al-maʿhūd / al-sujūd.

sentences.t: فَبَكَى وَقَالَ أَنَا لَا أُحْسِنُ شَيْأً مِنْ ذٰلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-bakā wa-qāla anā lā uḥsinu shayʾan min dhālika
sentences.l: And-he-wept and-said: I do-not do-well anything of that.
sentences.i: He wept and said, “I am no good at anything of the kind.”
sentences.n: aḥsana, Form IV, “to be good at, know how to do”: lā uḥsinu shayʾan min dhālika, “I have no skill in any of that”. The hamza of شيأ is printed on its alif seat, as in the verse above.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ بِحَيَاتِي أَنْ تَفْعَلَ مَا أَمَرْتُكَ بِهِ مِمَّا هُنَالِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat bi-ḥayātī an tafʿala mā amartuka bihi mimmā hunālika
sentences.l: And-she-said: By-my-life, that you-do what I-commanded-you with-it, of-what (is) there!
sentences.i: She said, “By my life, do what I have bidden you, with what is down there!”
sentences.n: bi-ḥayātī, “by my life”: bi- of the oath, here adjuring him. an tafʿala, “that you do”, with the subjunctive: the oath is followed by what is asked, as if “(I ask) that you do”; Classical usage would say illā faʿalta. amara bi-, “to command”: the verb chooses bi-, and bihi takes up mā. mimmā hunālika, “of what is there”, mimmā being min mā, points down to where his hand is to go.

sentences.t: فَمَدَّ يَدَهُ وَفُوأٰدُهُ فِي زَفِيرٍ فَوَجَدَ فَخِذَهَا أَلْيَنَ مِنَ الزُّبْدِ وَأَنْعَمَ مِنَ الْحَرِيرِ
sentences.tr: fa-madda yadahu wa-fuʾāduhu fī zafīrin fa-wajada fakhidhahā alyana mina al-zubdi wa-anʿama mina al-ḥarīri
sentences.l: And-he-stretched-out his-hand, and-his-heart (was) in sighing, and-found her-thigh softer than the-butter and-smoother than the-silk.
sentences.i: So he put out his hand, his heart heaving with sighs, and found her thigh softer than cream and smoother than silk.
sentences.n: The print has يدة, a misprint for يده, and وفوأدة, a misprint for وفوأده, both corrected here. fuʾād, “heart”, is spelt فوأد, with both the wāw seat of Classical فؤاد and a hamza on alif; the hamza is printed, and the word is read fuʾāduhu, the long ā shown by a dagger alif. wa-fuʾāduhu fī zafīrin, “his heart in sighing”, a circumstantial clause; zafīr, “a deep, heavy sigh”. wajada takes two objects: the thigh, and what he found it to be. alyan, “softer”, and anʿam, “smoother, more delicate”, are elatives: min marks what they are compared with. zubd, “fresh butter, cream”. The shadda of فمدّ is printed. The rhyme falls on zafīr / ḥarīr.

sentences.t: فَاسْتَلَذَّ بِلَمْسِهِمَا وَجَالَ بِيَدِهِ فِى الْجِهَاتِ حَتَّى وَصَلَتْ إِلَي قُبَّةٍ كَثِيرَةِ الْبَرَكَاتِ وَالْحَرَكَاتِ
sentences.tr: fa-istaladhdha bi-lamsihimā wa-jāla bi-yadihi fī al-jihāti ḥattā waṣalat ilā qubbatin kathīrati al-barakāti wa-al-ḥarakāti
sentences.l: And-he-took-pleasure in-touching-the-two, and-roamed with-his-hand in the-directions, until it-reached to a-dome abundant (in) the-blessings and-the-motions.
sentences.i: He took delight in the touch of them, and his hand roamed this way and that, until it came to a dome rich in blessings and in movements.
sentences.n: The print has بيدة, a misprint for بيده, corrected here. istaladhdha bi-, Form X of ladhdha, “to find pleasure in”: bi- marks the source of the pleasure; its shadda is printed. lamsihimā, “touching the two”: the dual takes in both her thighs, though only one was named. jāla bi-yadihi, “he roamed with his hand”: bi- marks the means. al-jihāt, “the sides, the directions”. waṣalat is feminine: its subject is his hand, yad. qubba, “dome”, is her mound and sex, in the euphemism of the tale; its shadda is printed. kathīrat al-barakāt, “abundant in blessings”, an adjective in construct with what it abounds in. فى is spelt with ى and الي with a dotted yāʾ, as the print has them. The rhyme falls on al-barakāt / al-ḥarakāt.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ لَعَلَّ هٰذَا الْمَلِكَ خُنْثَى وَلَيْسَ بِذَكَرٍ وَلَا أُنْثَى
sentences.tr: fa-qāla fī nafsihi laʿalla hādhā al-malika khunthā wa-laysa bi-dhakarin wa-lā unthā
sentences.l: And-he-said in himself: Perhaps this king (is) a-hermaphrodite, and-is-not a-male nor a-female.
sentences.i: He said to himself, “Perhaps this king is a hermaphrodite, neither male nor female.”
sentences.n: qāla fī nafsihi, “he said in himself”, that is, he thought. laʿalla takes the accusative, al-malika. khunthā, “hermaphrodite, one of both sexes or neither”, rhymes with unthā, “female”. laysa bi-dhakarin, “he is not a male”: the bi- after laysa only marks the predicate. The shadda of لعلّ is printed.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ إِنِّي لَمْ أَجِدْ لَكَ آلَةً مِثْلَ آلَاتِ الرِّجَالِ فَمَا حَمَلَكَ عَلَى هٰذِهِ الْفِعَالِ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla ayyuhā al-maliku innī lam ajid laka ālatan mithla ālāti al-rijāli fa-mā ḥamalaka ʿalā hādhihi al-fiʿāli
sentences.l: Then he-said: O-you the-king, indeed-I did-not find for-you a-tool like (the) tools (of) the-men; so what carried-you to these doings?
sentences.i: Then he said, “O king, I have found on you no member like the members of men. What has driven you to such doings?”
sentences.n: The print has هذة, a misprint for هذه, corrected here. āla, “tool, instrument”, here the male member: ālāt al-rijāl, “men's tools”; the madda of آلة and آلات is printed. lam ajid laka, “I did not find for you”: li- marks the one it should belong to. ḥamala ʿalā, “to drive, bring (someone) to”: ʿalā marks what one is driven to. fiʿāl, “deeds, doings”, rhymes with al-rijāl.

sentences.t: فَضَحِكَتِ الْمَلِكَةُ بُدُورُ حَتَّى اسْتَلْقَتْ عَلَى قَفَاهَا وَقَالَتْ لَهُ يَا حَبِيبِي مَا أَسْرَعَ مَا نَسِيتَ لَيَالِيًا بِتْنَاهَا
sentences.tr: fa-ḍaḥikati al-malikatu Budūru ḥattā istalqat ʿalā qafāhā wa-qālat lahu yā ḥabībī mā asraʿa mā nasīta layāliyan bitnāhā
sentences.l: And-laughed the-queen Budūr until she-lay-back on her-nape, and-said to-him: O my-beloved, how quick (is) what you-forgot nights we-spent-them!
sentences.i: Queen Budūr laughed until she fell back on the bed, and said to him, “My darling, how quickly you have forgotten the nights we spent together!”
sentences.n: istalqā ʿalā qafāhu, Form X, “to lie back on one's nape”, flat on one's back, the stock gesture of helpless laughter. mā asraʿa mā nasīta, “how quick is what you forgot!”, an exclamation: mā afʿala, “how …!”, with a second mā that turns the verb into a noun. layāliyan, “nights”: the print writes the alif of an indefinite accusative after layālī, which Classical Arabic would leave as layāliya, without tanwīn; it is vocalised as printed, a Middle Arabic form. bitnāhā, “we spent them”, from bāta, “to pass the night”: the nights of their marriage, before the stone parted them.

sentences.t: وَعَرَّفَتْهُ بِنَفْسِهَا فَعَرَفَ أَنَّهَا زَوْجَتُهُ الْمَلِكَةُ بُدُورُ بِنْتُ الْمَلِكِ الْغَيُورِ صَاحِبِ الْجَزَائِرِ وَالْبُحُورِ
sentences.tr: wa-ʿarrafathu bi-nafsihā fa-ʿarafa annahā zawjatuhu al-malikatu Budūru bintu al-maliki al-Ghayūri ṣāḥibi al-jazāʾiri wa-al-buḥūri
sentences.l: And-she-made-him-know of-herself, and-he-knew that-she (was) his-wife, the-queen Budūr, daughter (of) the-king al-Ghayūr, lord (of) the-islands and-the-seas.
sentences.i: Then she made herself known to him, and he knew that she was his wife, Queen Budūr, daughter of King al-Ghayūr, lord of the islands and the seas.
sentences.n: ʿarrafa bi-, Form II, “to make (someone) acquainted with”: bi- marks what is made known, here herself; its shadda is printed. al-Ghayūr, “the Jealous”, her father's name. ṣāḥib, “owner, lord”. buḥūr, a plural of baḥr, “sea”, beside the commoner biḥār, rhymes with al-Ghayūr. The hamza of الجزائر is printed.

sentences.t: فَاحْتَضَنَهَا وَاحْتَضَنَتْهُ وَقَبَّلَهَا وَقَبَّلَتْهُ ثُمَّ اضْطَجَعَا عَلَى فِرَاشِ الْوِصَالِ وَتَنَاشَدَا قَوْلَ مَنْ قَالَ
sentences.tr: fa-iḥtaḍanahā wa-iḥtaḍanathu wa-qabbalahā wa-qabbalathu thumma iḍṭajaʿā ʿalā firāshi al-wiṣāli wa-tanāshadā qawla man qāla
sentences.l: And-he-embraced-her and-she-embraced-him, and-he-kissed-her and-she-kissed-him; then the-two-lay-down on (the) bed (of) the-union, and-recited-to-each-other (the) saying (of) one-who said:
sentences.i: He took her in his arms and she him, he kissed her and she him; then they lay down together on the bed of union, and recited to each other the words of the poet:
sentences.n: iḥtaḍana, Form VIII, “to clasp to the breast”. The paired verbs, his and hers, mirror one another; the shaddas of قبّلها and قبّلته are printed. iḍṭajaʿa, Form VIII of ḍajaʿa, “to lie down”, here dual. firāsh al-wiṣāl, “the bed of union”, where lovers are joined. tanāshada, Form VI of nashada, “to recite verses to one another”, dual.

sentences.t:
لَمَّا دَعَتْهُ اِلَى وِصَالِيْ عِطْفَةٌ * مِنْ مَعْطَفٍ بِتَعَطُّفٍ مُتَوَاصِ
وَسَقَتْ قَسَاوَةَ قَلْبِهِ مِنْ لِيْنِهَا * فَاَجَابَ بَعْدَ تَمَنُّعٍ وَتَعَاصِ
خَشِيَ الْعَوَاذِلَ اَنْ تَرَاهُ اِذَا بَدَا * فَاَتَى بِعُدَّةِ آمِنِ الْاِرْهَاصِ
شَكَتِ الْخُصُوْرُ رَوَادِفًا قَدْ حَمَّلَتْ * اَقْدَامَهُ فِى الْمَشْيِ حِمْلَ قِلَاصِ
مُتَقَلِّدُ الصَّمْصَامِ مِنْ اَلْحَاظِهِ * وَمِنَ الدُّجَى مُتَدَرِّعًا بِدِلَاصِ
وَشَذَاهُ بَشَّرَنِي بِسَعْدِ قُدُوْمِهِ * فَفَرَرْتُ مِثْلَ الطَّيْرِ مِنْ اَقْفَاصِ
وَفَرَشْتُ خَدِّيْ فِى الطَّرِيْقِ لِنَعْلِهِ * فَشَفَى بِاِثْمِدِ تُرْبِهَا اَرْمَاصِي
وَعَقَدْتُ الْوِيَةَ الْوِصَالِ مُعَانِقًا * وَفَكَكْتُ عُقْدَةَ حَظِّيَ الْمُتَعَاصِى
وَاَقَمْتُ اَفْرَاحًا اَجَابَ نِدَائَهَا * طَرِبٌ صَفَا عَنْ شَائِبِ الْاَنْغَاصِ
وَالْبَدْرُ نَقَّطَ بِالنُّجُوْمِ الثَّغْرَ مِنْ * حَبَبٍ عَلَى وَجْهِ الطِّلَا رَقَّاصِ
وَعَكَفْتُ فِي مِحْرَابِ لَذَّتِهَا عَلَى * مَا مِنْ تَعَاطِيهِ يَتُوْبُ الْعَاصِى
قَسَمًا بِاَيَاتِ الضُّحَى مِنْ وَجْهِهِ * لَمْ اَنْسَ فِيْهِ سُوْرَةَ الْاِخْلَاصِ
sentences.tr:
lammā daʿathu ilā wiṣālī ʿiṭfatun * min maʿṭafin bi-taʿaṭṭufin mutawāṣi
wa-saqat qasāwata qalbihi min līnihā * fa-ajāba baʿda tamannuʿin wa-taʿāṣi
khashiya al-ʿawādhila an tarāhu idhā badā * fa-atā bi-ʿuddati āmini al-irhāṣi
shakati al-khuṣūru rawādifan qad ḥammalat * aqdāmahu fī al-mashyi ḥimla qilāṣi
mutaqallidu al-ṣamṣāmi min alḥāẓihi * wa-mina al-dujā mutadarriʿan bi-dilāṣi
wa-shadhāhu bashsharanī bi-saʿdi qudūmihi * fa-farartu mithla al-ṭayri min aqfāṣi
wa-farashtu khaddī fī al-ṭarīqi li-naʿlihi * fa-shafā bi-ithmidi turbihā armāṣī
wa-ʿaqadtu alwiyata al-wiṣāli muʿāniqan * wa-fakaktu ʿuqdata ḥaẓẓiya al-mutaʿāṣī
wa-aqamtu afrāḥan ajāba nidāʾahā * ṭaribun ṣafā ʿan shāʾibi al-anghāṣi
wa-al-badru naqqaṭa bi-al-nujūmi al-thaghra min * ḥababin ʿalā wajhi al-ṭilā raqqāṣi
wa-ʿakaftu fī miḥrābi ladhdhatihā ʿalā * mā min taʿāṭīhi yatūbu al-ʿāṣī
qasaman bi-āyāti al-ḍuḥā min wajhihi * lam ansa fīhi sūrata al-ikhlāṣi
sentences.l:
When called-him to union-with-me a-bending * from a-supple-waist with-tender-inclining unceasing,
and-it-gave-to-drink (the) hardness (of) his-heart from its-softness, * he-answered after holding-back and-resisting.
He-feared the-blamers, that they-see-him when he-appeared, * so-he-came with-(the)-gear (of one) safe (from) the-forewarning.
Complained the-waists (of) hips that had-laden * his-feet in the-walking (with the) load (of) young-she-camels.
Girded (with) the-keen-sword from his-glances, * and-from the-dark clad with-smooth-mail.
And-his-fragrance gave-me-tidings of-(the)-good-fortune (of) his-coming, * and-I-flew like the-birds from cages.
And-I-spread my-cheek on the-road for-his-sandal, * and-healed with-(the)-kohl (of) its-dust my-sore-eyes.
And-I-knotted (the) banners (of) the-union, embracing, * and-I-untied (the) knot (of) my-fortune the-stubborn.
And-I-held rejoicings — answered their-call * one-merry, clear of (the) taint (of) the-troubles.
And-the-full-moon dotted with-the-stars the-mouth, of * bubbles on (the) face (of) the-wine dancing.
And-I-kept-devout in (the) prayer-niche (of) its-pleasure upon * what by practising-it repents the-sinner.
An-oath by-(the)-verses (of) the-morning-brightness from his-face: * I-did-not forget in-it (the) sura (of) the-Sincerity.
sentences.i:
When a tender bending of a supple waist, * with kindness that would not cease, called him to my embrace,
and gave the hardness of his heart its softness to drink, * he answered, after holding back and resisting.
He feared the censurers might see him when he showed himself, * and came armed like one who fears no warning sign.
Waists complained of the hips that weighed down * his feet as he walked, as with the load of young camels.
He wore the sword of his glances at his side, * and the dark of night as a coat of shining mail.
His fragrance brought me news of his happy coming, * and I flew out like a bird from its cage.
I spread my cheek on the road for his sandal, * and the kohl of its dust healed my sore eyes.
I knotted the banners of union as I held him, * and untied the knot of my stubborn fortune.
I held a feast of joy, and its call was answered * by a delight unclouded by any trouble.
The full moon had dotted the mouth with stars * of bubbles dancing on the face of the wine.
In the prayer-niche of its pleasure I gave myself up * to that by whose practice the sinner repents.
I swear by the verses of morning light in his face: * I did not forget there the Sura of Sincerity.
sentences.n: The verses are pointed in the print and copied as printed. The metre is kāmil, and every line rhymes in -āṣi; to keep the rhyme the print drops the final yāʾ of mutawāṣī and taʿāṣī, writing مُتَوَاصِ and تَعَاصِ. The beloved is “he”, as in most love poetry, and the speaker “I”; the two lovers recite it together. The first line plays on one root: ʿiṭfa, “a bending, a kind turning”, maʿṭaf, “the side, the supple waist”, taʿaṭṭuf, “tender inclining”. tamannuʿ and taʿāṣī, “holding back” and “resisting”, are Forms V and VI. In the third line āmin al-irhāṣ is obscure: irhāṣ, Form IV of rahaṣa, is a foundation, or the portent that goes before an event; “one safe from forewarning” is a guess at the sense, that he came prepared like a man who fears no sign will give him away. rawādif, “hips, buttocks”, the heavy haunches the poets prize beside a slender waist; qilāṣ, plural of qalūṣ, “young she-camel”. ṣamṣām, “a keen sword”; alḥāẓ, “glances”; dilāṣ, “smooth, shining mail”: his glances are his sword, the night his armour. shadhā, “fragrance”. ithmid, “antimony, kohl”, and armāṣ, plural of ramaṣ, “matter in the corner of the eye”: the dust of his sandal is a salve for sore eyes; -hā in turbihā goes back to the sandal, naʿl, which is feminine. In the eighth line the print sets الْوِيَةَ with a bare alif and a sukūn on the lām, as if it were the article: alwiya, “banners”, plural of liwāʾ, loses its hamza for the metre. ḥaẓẓiya, “my fortune”, is printed with a fatḥa on the yāʾ. نِدَائَهَا, nidāʾahā, “its call”, is printed with the hamza on a yāʾ seat. ṭarib, “one moved to delight”; shāʾib, “admixture, taint”; anghāṣ, plural of naghaṣ, “what spoils a pleasure”. The tenth line is crowded and its picture uncertain: the moon, the beloved's face, has dotted “the mouth” with stars, which seem to be the bubbles, ḥabab, dancing on the face of the wine, ṭilā, as his teeth shine in his smile. In the eleventh, ʿakafa ʿalā, “to keep devoutly to”, and miḥrāb, “prayer-niche”, make love a worship: by this practice, taʿāṭī, the sinner turns penitent. -hā in ladhdhatihā most likely goes back to the wine, though the poem leaves it open. The last line puns on two suras of the Qurʾan: al-Ḍuḥā, “The Morning Brightness” (93), whose āyāt, “verses”, are also the “signs” of light in his face, and al-Ikhlāṣ, “Sincerity” (112), here his faithfulness; the print writes āyāt with a fatḥa on a bare alif, بِاَيَاتِ. The print writes a bare alif without hamza in many words (اِلَى, فَاَجَابَ, اَنْ, اِذَا, فَاَتَى, الْاِرْهَاصِ, اَقْدَامَهُ, اَلْحَاظِهِ, اَقْفَاصِ, بِاِثْمِدِ, اَرْمَاصِي, وَاَقَمْتُ, اَفْرَاحًا, اَجَابَ, الْاَنْغَاصِ, اَنْسَ, الْاِخْلَاصِ), ى for final ī in فِى, الْمُتَعَاصِى and الْعَاصِى, and a sukūn on many long vowels; all are kept.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمَلِكَةَ بُدُورَ أَخْبَرَتْ قَمَرَ الزَّمَانِ بِجَمِيعِ مَا جَرَى لَهَا مِنَ الْأَوَّلِ إِلَى الْآخِرِ وَكَذٰلِكَ هُوَ أَخْبَرَهَا بِجَمِيعِ مَاجَرَى لَهُ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-malikata Budūra akhbarat Qamara al-Zamāni bi-jamīʿi mā jarā lahā mina al-awwali ilā al-ākhiri wa-ka-dhālika huwa akhbarahā bi-jamīʿi mā jarā lahu
sentences.l: Then indeed the-queen Budūr informed Qamar al-Zamān of-all what happened to-her from the-first to the-last; and-likewise he informed-her of-all what happened to-him.
sentences.i: Then Queen Budūr told Qamar al-Zamān all that had befallen her from first to last, and he likewise told her all that had befallen him.
sentences.n: thumma inna, the narrator's “then”. akhbara bi-, Form IV, “to inform (someone) of”: the verb chooses bi-. jarā li-, “to happen to”: li- marks the one it befalls. The print sets mā jarā solid as ماجرى the second time, kept so. The madda of الآخر is printed. ka-dhālika, “likewise”: ka-, “like”, + dhālika, “that”.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ انْتَقَلَ مَعَهَا إِلَى الْعِتَابِ وَقَالَ لَهَا مَا حَمَلَكِ عَلَى مَا فَعَلْتِهِ بِي فِي هٰذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda dhālika intaqala maʿahā ilā al-ʿitābi wa-qāla lahā mā ḥamalaki ʿalā mā faʿaltihi bī fī hādhihi al-laylati
sentences.l: And-after that he-moved-on with-her to the-reproaching, and-said to-her: What carried-you (f.) to what you-(f.)-did-it with-me in this night?
sentences.i: After that he turned to reproaching her, and said, “What made you do what you did to me tonight?”
sentences.n: The print has هذة, a misprint for هذه, corrected here. intaqala ilā, Form VIII, “to move on to”. ʿitāb, “loving reproach”. The print itself sets the kasra of the feminine “you” in حملكِ and فعلتِه, so that no one reads the masculine he used to the king: now he speaks to a woman. ḥamala ʿalā, as before, “to drive to”. faʿala bi-: bi- marks the one it is done to.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَا تُؤَاخِذْنِي فَإِنَّ قَصْدِي بِذٰلِكَ الْمِزَاحُ وَمَزِيدُ الْبَسْطِ وَالِانْشِرَاحِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lā tuʾākhidhnī fa-inna qaṣdī bi-dhālika al-mizāḥu wa-mazīdu al-basṭi wa-al-inshirāḥi
sentences.l: And-she-said: Do-not take-me-to-task, for indeed my-intent by-that (was) the-jesting and-increase (of) the-cheer and-the-gladness.
sentences.i: She said, “Do not hold it against me: I meant it only in jest, and for the more merriment and delight.”
sentences.n: ākhadha, Form III, “to take (someone) to task, blame”, jussive after lā of prohibition; its hamza is printed, ؤ. qaṣdī bi-dhālika, “my intention by that”: bi- marks the act meant. mizāḥ, “jesting”; mazīd, “increase, a further measure”; basṭ, “expansiveness, good cheer”; inshirāḥ, Form VII, “the opening of the breast”, gladness. The rhyme falls on al-mizāḥ / al-inshirāḥ, and runs on into the daybreak formula that follows.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ وَأَضَاءَ بِنُورِهِ وَلَاحَ أَرْسَلَتِ الْمَلِكَةُ بُدُورُ إِلَى الْمَلِكِ أَرْمَانُوسَ وَالِدِ الْمَلِكَةِ حَيَاةِ النُّفُوسِ وَأَخْبَرَتْهُ بِحَقِيقَةِ أَمْرِهَا وَأَنَّهَا زَوْجَةُ قَمَرِ الزَّمَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu wa-aḍāʾa bi-nūrihi wa-lāḥa arsalati al-malikatu Budūru ilā al-maliki Armānūsa wālidi al-malikati Ḥayāti al-Nufūsi wa-akhbarathu bi-ḥaqīqati amrihā wa-annahā zawjatu Qamari al-Zamāni
sentences.l: And-when dawned the-morning and-shone with-its-light and-gleamed, sent the-queen Budūr to the-king Armānūs, (the) father (of) the-queen Ḥayāt al-Nufūs, and-informed-him of-(the)-truth (of) her-affair, and-that-she (was the) wife (of) Qamar al-Zamān.
sentences.i: When morning came and shone out in its light, Queen Budūr sent for King Armānūs, the father of Queen Ḥayāt al-Nufūs, and told him the truth about herself, and that she was the wife of Qamar al-Zamān.
sentences.n: The print has بنورة, a misprint for بنوره, corrected here. fa-lammā aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu wa-aḍāʾa bi-nūrihi wa-lāḥa, “when morning dawned and shone with its light and gleamed”, the storyteller's rhymed formula for daybreak: bi- marks that with which it shines. The ء of واضاء is printed. arsala ilā, “to send to”, here “to send for”. wālid, “father”. Ḥayāt al-Nufūs is called malika, “queen”, as a king's daughter and the wife of the king of the Isles. akhbara bi-: the verb chooses bi-, and wa-annahā, “and that she”, adds a second thing told. Armānūs is diptote: Armānūsa, genitive.

sentences.t: وَأَخْبَرَتْهُ بِقِصَّتِهِمَا وَبِسَبَبِ افْتِرَاقِهِمَا مِنْ بَعْضِهِمَا وَأَعْلَمَتْهُ أَنَّ ابْنَتَهُ حَيَاةَ النُّفُوسِ بِكْرٌ عَلَى حَالِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-akhbarathu bi-qiṣṣatihimā wa-bi-sababi iftirāqihimā min baʿḍihimā wa-aʿlamathu anna ibnatahu Ḥayāta al-Nufūsi bikrun ʿalā ḥālihā
sentences.l: And-she-informed-him of-their-story and-of-(the)-cause (of) their-parting from each-other, and-made-known-to-him that his-daughter Ḥayāt al-Nufūs (was) a-virgin on her-state.
sentences.i: She told him their story and how they had come to be parted from each other, and let him know that his daughter Ḥayāt al-Nufūs was still a virgin, as she had been.
sentences.n: bi- marks what is told after akhbara, twice: bi-qiṣṣatihimā, “of their story”, and bi-sababi, “of the cause”. iftirāq min baʿḍihimā, “their parting from one another”: min baʿḍ for “from each other” is the later language's idiom. aʿlama, Form IV, “to let (someone) know”. bikr, “virgin”. ʿalā ḥālihā, “on her (former) state”, that is, untouched as she was.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْمَلِكُ أَرْمَانُوسُ صَاحِبُ جَزَائِرِ الْآبَنُوسِ قِصَّةَ الْمَلِكَةِ بُدُورَ بِنْتِ الْمَلِكِ الْغَيُورِ تَعَجَّبَ مِنْهَا غَايَةَ الْعَجَبِ وَأَمَرَ أَنْ يَكْتُبُوهَا بِمَاءِ الذَّهَبِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-maliku Armānūsu ṣāḥibu Jazāʾiri al-Ābanūsi qiṣṣata al-malikati Budūra binti al-maliki al-Ghayūri taʿajjaba minhā ghāyata al-ʿajabi wa-amara an yaktubūhā bi-māʾi al-dhahabi
sentences.l: And-when heard the-king Armānūs, lord (of the) Isles (of) the-Ebony, (the) story (of) the-queen Budūr, daughter (of) the-king al-Ghayūr, he-marvelled at-it (the) utmost (of) the-marvelling, and-commanded that they-write-it with-water (of) the-gold.
sentences.i: When King Armānūs, lord of the Ebony Isles, heard the story of Queen Budūr, daughter of King al-Ghayūr, he marvelled at it beyond measure, and commanded that it be written down in letters of gold.
sentences.n: taʿajjaba min, Form V, “to wonder at”: min marks what is wondered at; its shadda is printed. ghāyata al-ʿajabi, “the utmost of wonder”, an accusative that measures the verb. amara an, “to command that”, with the subjunctive; “they” are the scribes. bi-māʾi al-dhahabi, “with water of gold”, that is, in liquid gold: bi- marks what it is written with. The rhyme al-ʿajab / al-dhahab is the stock close for a tale worth keeping. Budūra, genitive after qiṣṣata, is diptote. The madda of الآبنوس and the hamza of جزائر are printed.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ الْتَفَتَ إِلَى قَمَرِ الزَّمَانِ وَقَالَ لَهُ يَا ابْنَ الْمَلِكِ هَلْ لَكَ أَنْ تُصَاهِرَنِي وَتَتَزَوَّجَ بِنْتِي حَيَاةَ النُّفُوسِ
sentences.tr: thumma iltafata ilā Qamari al-Zamāni wa-qāla lahu yā ibna al-maliki hal laka an tuṣāhiranī wa-tatazawwaja bintī Ḥayāta al-Nufūsi
sentences.l: Then he-turned to Qamar al-Zamān and-said to-him: O son (of) the-king, is-there for-you that you-become-my-kin-by-marriage and-marry my-daughter Ḥayāt al-Nufūs?
sentences.i: Then he turned to Qamar al-Zamān and said to him, “Son of a king, will you become my kinsman by marriage, and take my daughter Ḥayāt al-Nufūs to wife?”
sentences.n: iltafata ilā, Form VIII, “to turn toward”. hal laka an, “is there for you that”, a courteous “would you be willing to”: li- marks the one whose wish is asked. ṣāhara, Form III, from ṣihr, “kin by marriage”, “to marry into (someone's) family”; tazawwaja, Form V, “to marry”, here with a direct object.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ حَتَّى أُشَاوِرَ الْمَلِكَةَ بُدُورَ فَإِنَّ لَهَا عَلَيَّ فَضْلًا غَيْرَ مَحْصُورٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu ḥattā ushāwira al-malikata Budūra fa-inna lahā ʿalayya faḍlan ghayra maḥṣūrin
sentences.l: And-he-said to-him: Until I-consult the-queen Budūr; for indeed for-her upon-me (is) a-favour not confined.
sentences.i: He said, “Not until I have consulted Queen Budūr, for I owe her more kindness than can be counted.”
sentences.n: ḥattā ushāwira, “until I consult”, with the subjunctive: an answer that holds back its assent, “(I cannot say) until I have asked her”. shāwara, Form III, “to consult”. lahā ʿalayya faḍlun, “she has a favour over me”: li- marks the one to whom it is owed, ʿalā the one who owes it; the shadda of عليّ is printed. ghayr maḥṣūr, “not to be confined”, beyond counting. The rhyme falls on Budūr / maḥṣūr.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا شَاوَرَهَا قَالَتْ لَهُ نَعَمْ هٰذَا الرَّأْيُ فَتَزَوَّجْهَا وَأَكُونُ أَنَا لَهَا جَارِيَةً لِأَنَّ لَهَا عَلَيَّ مَعْرُوفًا وَإِحْسَانًا وَخَيْرًا وَامْتِنَانًا وَخُصُوصًا نَحْنُ فِي مَحَلِّهَا وَقَدْ غَمَرَنَا إِحْسَانُ أَبِيهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā shāwarahā qālat lahu naʿam hādhā al-raʾyu fa-tazawwajhā wa-akūnu anā lahā jāriyatan li-anna lahā ʿalayya maʿrūfan wa-iḥsānan wa-khayran wa-imtinānan wa-khuṣūṣan naḥnu fī maḥallihā wa-qad ghamaranā iḥsānu abīhā
sentences.l: And-when he-consulted-her, she-said to-him: Yes, this (is) the-(right)-counsel; so-marry-her, and-I-shall-be, I, to-her a-slave-girl, because for-her upon-me (is) kindness and-beneficence and-good and-bounty; and-especially we (are) in her-place, and-already has-flooded-us (the) beneficence (of) her-father.
sentences.i: When he consulted her, she said, “Yes, that is the right course. Marry her, and I will be her handmaid; for I owe her kindness and goodness, generosity and grace, all the more as we are in her home, and her father's bounty has been showered upon us.”
sentences.n: hādhā al-raʾyu, “this is the (sound) counsel”; the hamza of الرأي is printed. fa-tazawwajhā, “so marry her”, imperative; its shadda is printed. wa-akūnu, “and I shall be”, indicative, a plain promise. jāriya, “slave-girl, handmaid”: the first wife offers to serve the second, a courtesy, not a demotion. li-anna, “because”; lahā ʿalayya, “she has over me”, as above, with the printed shadda of عليّ. maʿrūf, “kindness”, iḥsān, “beneficence”, khayr, “good”, imtinān, “bounty, favour”: a rhyming list, iḥsānan / imtinānan. wa-khuṣūṣan naḥnu, “and especially (as) we are”, a Middle Arabic turn: khuṣūṣan followed by a bare nominal clause. maḥall, “place, home”; its shadda is printed. ghamara, “to flood, overwhelm”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَى قَمَرُ الزَّمَانِ أَنَّ الْمَلِكَةَ بُدُورَ مَائِلَةٌ إِلَى ذٰلِكَ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ عِنْدَهَا غَيْرَةٌ مِنْ حَيَاةِ النُّفُوسِ اتَّفَقَ مَعَهَا عَلَى هٰذَا الْأَمْرِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾā Qamaru al-Zamāni anna al-malikata Budūra māʾilatun ilā dhālika wa-lam yakun ʿindahā ghayratun min Ḥayāti al-Nufūsi ittafaqa maʿahā ʿalā hādhā al-amri
sentences.l: And-when saw Qamar al-Zamān that the-queen Budūr (was) inclining to that, and-there-was-not with-her jealousy of Ḥayāt al-Nufūs, he-agreed with-her on this matter.
sentences.i: When Qamar al-Zamān saw that Queen Budūr was inclined to it, and felt no jealousy of Ḥayāt al-Nufūs, he agreed with her on the matter.
sentences.n: māʾila ilā, “inclining toward”, active participle of māla; its hamza is printed, as is that of رأى. lam yakun ʿindahā ghayratun, “there was not with her any jealousy”: yakun is masculine, though ghayra is feminine, as often when the verb comes first and is separated from its subject. ghayra min, “jealousy of”: min marks the rival. ittafaqa maʿa … ʿalā, Form VIII, “to agree with (someone) on (something)”: ʿalā marks the matter; its shadda is printed.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the-morning overtook Shahrazād, and-she-fell-silent from the-permitted speech.
sentences.i: And morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the speech allowed her.
sentences.n: The closing formula, as at the end of every night. The rhyme falls on al-ṣabāḥ / al-mubāḥ.
